1.1: Blessed is the man, that goeth not in the counsel of wicked men; and stood not in the way of sinners, and sat not in the chair of pestilence.
1.2: But his will is in the law of the Lord; and he shall bethink in the law of him day and night.
1.3: And he shall be as a tree, which is planted beside the runnings of waters; that shall give his fruit in his time. And his leaf shall not fall down; and all things, whichever he shall do, shall have prosperity.
1.4: Not so wicked men, not so; but they be as dust, which the wind casteth away from the face of the earth.
1.5: Therefore wicked men rise not again in doom; neither sinners in the council of just men [[nor the sinful in the council of the rightwise]].
1.6: For the Lord knoweth the way of just men [[or the rightwise]]; and the way of wicked men shall perish.

2.1: Why gnashed with teeth heathen men; and peoples thought vain things?
2.2: The kings of earth stood together; and princes came together against the Lord, and against his Christ.
2.3: Break we the bonds of them; and cast we away the yoke of them from us.
2.4: He that dwelleth in heavens shall scorn them; and the Lord shall bemock them.
2.5: Then he shall speak to them in his wrath; and he shall trouble them in his strong vengeance.
2.6: Soothly I am ordained of him a king upon Zion, his holy hill;
2.7: preaching his commandment. The Lord said to me, Thou art my son; I have begotten thee today.
2.8: Ask thou of me, and I shall give to thee heathen men for thine heritage; and for thy possession the terms of earth.
2.9: Thou shalt govern them in an iron rod; and thou shalt break them altogether as the vessel of a potter.
2.10: And now, ye kings, understand; ye that deem the earth, be ye learned.
2.11: Serve ye the Lord with dread; and make ye full out joy to him with trembling.
2.12: Take ye lore of chastising; lest the Lord be wroth sometime, and ye perish from the just way. When his wrath shall burn out in short time; blessed be all they, that trust in him.

3.1: The psalm of David, when he fled from the face of Absalom, his son. Lord, why be they multiplied that trouble me? many men rise against me.
3.2: Many men say of my soul, None health there is to him in his God.
3.3: But thou, Lord, art mine up-taker; my glory, and enhancing mine head.
3.4: With my voice I cried to the Lord; and he heard me from his holy hill.
3.5: I slept, and rested, and I rose up; for the Lord received me.
3.6: I shall not dread thousands of people encompassing me;
3.7: Lord, arise thou; my God, make me safe. For thou hast smitten all men being adversaries to me without cause; thou hast all-broken the teeth of sinners.
3.8: Health is of the Lord; and thy blessing is on thy people.

4.1: To the victory, in organs, the psalm of David. When I inwardly called, God of my rightwiseness heard me; in tribulation thou hast alarged to me. Have thou mercy on me; and hear thou my prayer.
4.2: Sons of men, how long be ye of heavy heart? why love ye vanity, and seek leasing?
4.3: And know ye, that the Lord hath made marvellous his holy man; the Lord shall hear me, when I shall cry to him.
4.4: Be ye wroth, and do not ye sin; and for those evils to which ye say in your hearts and in your beds, be ye compunct.
4.5: Sacrifice ye the sacrifice or Offer ye an offering of rightfulness [[or right-wiseness]], and hope ye in the Lord;
4.6: many say, Who showed good things to us? Lord, the light of thy cheer is marked upon us;
4.7: thou hast given gladness in mine heart. They be multiplied of the fruit of wheat, and of wine; and of their oil.
4.8: In peace in the same thing; I shall sleep, and take rest. For thou, Lord; hast set me singularly or only in hope.

5.1: To the overcomer, on the heritages, the psalm of David. Lord, perceive thou my words with ears; understand thou my cry.
5.2: My King, and my God; give thou attention to the voice of my prayer. For, Lord, I shall pray to thee;
5.3: hear thou early my voice. Early I shall stand nigh to thee, and I shall see;
5.4: for thou art God not desiring wickedness. Neither an evil-willed man shall dwell beside thee;
5.5: neither unjust [[or unrightwise]] men shall dwell before thine eyes. Thou hatest all them that work wickedness;
5.6: thou shalt lose them that speak leasing. The Lord shall hold abomin-able a man-queller, and a guileful man.
5.7: But Lord, in the multitude of thy mercy, I shall enter into thine house; I shall worship toward thine holy temple in thy dread.
5.8: Lord, lead thou forth me in thy rightwiseness for mine enemies; dress thou my way in thy sight.
5.9: For truth is not in their mouth; their heart is vain. Their throat is an open sepulchre, they did guilefully with their tongues;
5.10: God, deem thou them. Fall they down from their thoughts; after the multitude of their wickednesses, or un-piousnesses, cast thou them down; for, Lord, they have stirred thee to wrath.
5.11: And all that hope in thee, be they glad; they shall make full out joy [[into]] without end, and thou shalt dwell in them. And all that love thy name shall have glory in thee;
5.12: for thou shalt bless the just [[or right-wise]] man. Lord, thou hast crowned us, as with a shield of thy good will.

6.1: To the overcomer in psalms, the psalm of David, on the eighth. Lord, reprove thou not me in thy strong vengeance; neither chastise thou me in thine ire.
6.2: Lord, have thou mercy on me, for I am sick; Lord, make thou me whole, for all my bones be troubled.
6.3: And my soul is troubled greatly; but thou, Lord, how long?
6.4: Lord, be thou converted or turned again, and deliver my soul; make thou me safe, for thy mercy.
6.5: For none there is in death, that is mindful of thee; but in hell who shall acknowledge to thee?
6.6: I travailed in my wailing, I shall wash my bed by each night; I shall moisten, either make wet, my bedstraw with my tears.
6.7: Mine eye is troubled of strong vengeance; I waxed eld or old among all mine enemies.
6.8: All ye that work wickedness, depart from me; for the Lord hath heard the voice of my weeping.
6.9: The Lord hath heard my beseech-ing; the Lord hath received my prayer.
6.10: All mine enemies be ashamed, and be troubled greatly; be they turned altogether, and be they ashamed full swiftly.

7.1: For the ignorance of David, which he sang to the Lord, on the words of Ethiopian, the son of Benjamin. My Lord God, I have hoped in thee; make thou me safe from all that pursue me, and deliver thou me.
7.2: Lest any time he as a lion ravish my soul; while none there is that again-buyeth, neither that maketh safe.
7.3: My Lord God, if I did this thing, if wickedness is in mine hands, or works;
7.4: if I yielded to men yielding to me evils, fall I by deserving void from mine enemies;
7.5: mine enemy pursue he my soul, and take he, and defoul my life in earth; and bring my glory into dust.
7.6: Lord, rise thou up in thine ire; and be thou raised up in the coasts of mine enemies. And, my Lord God, rise thou up in the commandment, which thou hast commanded;
7.7: and the synagogue of peoples shall encompass thee. And for this go thou again on high;
7.8: the Lord deemeth peoples. Lord, deem thou me by my rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]]; and by mine innocence on me.
7.9: The wickedness of sinners be ended; and thou, God, seeking the hearts, that is, thoughts, and reins, that is, delightings, shall dress a just [[or rightwise]] man.
7.10: My just [[or rightwise]] help is of the Lord; that maketh safe rightful men in heart.
7.11: The Lord is a just [[or rightwise]] judge, strong and patient; whether he is wroth by all days?
7.12: If ye be not converted, he shall flourish his sword; he hath bent his bow, and made it ready.
7.13: And therein he hath made ready the vessels of death; he hath fully made his arrows with burning things.
7.14: Lo! the wicked hath conceived sorrow; he painfully hath brought forth unrightfulness [[or unrightwiseness]], and he hath childed wickedness.
7.15: He opened a pit, and digged it out; and he fell into the ditch which he made.
7.16: His sorrow shall be turned into his head; and his wickedness shall come down into his neck.
7.17: I shall acknowledge to the Lord by his rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]]; and I shall sing to the name of the highest Lord.

8.1: To the overcomer, for [[the]] pressers [[or wine presses]], the psalm of David. Lord, thou art our Lord; thy name is full wonderful in all [[the]] earth. For thy great doing is raised up, above heavens.
8.2: Of the mouth of young children, not speaking and sucking milk, thou hast made perfect praising, for thine enemies; that thou destroy the enemy and the avenger.
8.3: For I shall see thine heavens, the works of thy fingers; the moon and the stars, which thou hast founded.
8.4: What is a man, that is mankind, that thou art mindful of him; either the son of a virgin [[or the son of man]], for thou visitest him?
8.5: Thou hast made him a little less than angels; thou hast crowned him with glory and honour,
8.6: and thou hast ordained him above the works of thine hands. Thou hast made subject all things under his feet;
8.7: all sheep and oxen, furthermore and the beasts of the field;
8.8: the birds of the air, and the fishes of the sea, and all the other creatures that pass by the paths of the sea.
8.9: Lord, our Lord; how wonderful is thy name in all [[the]] earth.

9.1: Into the end, for the privates of the son, the psalm of David. Lord, I shall acknowledge to thee in all mine heart; I shall tell all thy marvels.
9.2: Thou Highest, I shall be glad, and I shall be fully joyful [[or full out joy]] in thee; I shall sing to thy name.
9.3: For thou turnest mine enemy aback; they shall be made feeble, and shall perish from thy face.
9.4: For thou hast made my doom, and my cause; thou, that deemest rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]], hast set on the throne.
9.5: Thou hast blamed heathen men, and the wicked perished; thou hast done away the name of them into the world, and into the world of world.
9.6: The swords of the enemy have failed into the end; and thou hast destroyed the cities of them. The mind of them hath perished with sound;
9.7: and the Lord dwelleth without end. He hath made ready his throne in doom;
9.8: and he shall deem the world in equity, he shall deem peoples in rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]].
9.9: And the Lord is made refuge, either help, to a poor man; an helper in covenable times in tribulation.
9.10: And they, that know thy name, have hope in thee; for thou, Lord, hast not forsaken them that seek thee.
9.11: Sing ye [[psalms]] to the Lord, that dwelleth in Zion; tell ye his studies among heathen men.
9.12: God forgetteth not the cry of poor men; for he hath mind of them, and he seeketh the blood of them.
9.13: Lord, have thou mercy on me; see thou my meekness of mine enemies. Which enhancest me from the gates of death;
9.14: that I tell all thy praisings in the gates of the daughter of Zion. I shall be fully joyful or joy fully in thine health;
9.15: heathen men be fast-set in the perishing, which they made. In this snare, which they hid, the foot of them is caught.
9.16: The Lord making dooms shall be known; the sinner is taken in the works of his hands.
9.17: Sinners be turned altogether into hell; all folks, that forget God.
9.18: For the forgetting of a poor man shall not be into the end; the patience of poor men shall not perish into the end.
9.19: Lord, rise thou up, a man be not comforted; [[the]] folks be deemed in thy sight.
9.20: Lord, ordain thou a law-maker upon them; know folks, that they be men.

10.1: Lord, why hast thou gone far away? thou despisest us in covenable times in tribulation.
10.2: While the wicked man waxeth proud, the poor man is burnt; they be taken in the wicked counsels, which they thinked.
10.3: For why the sinner is praised in the desires of his soul; and the wicked is blessed. The sinner hath stirred the Lord to wrath;
10.4: after the multitude of his wrath, he shall not seek after God. God is not in his sight;
10.5: his ways be defouled in all time. Thy dooms be taken away from his face; he shall be lord of all his enemies.
10.6: For he said in his heart, I shall not be moved, from generation into gener-ation without evil.
10.7: Whose mouth is full of cursing, and of bitterness, and of guile; travail and sorrow is under his tongue.
10.8: He sitteth in ambushes with rich men in privates; to slay the innocent man. His eyes behold cruelly on the poor man;
10.9: he setteth ambushes in hid place, as a lion in his den. He setteth ambushes, for to ravish a poor man; for to ravish a poor man, while he draweth in the poor man. In his snare he shall make meek the poor man;
10.10: he shall bow himself down, and he shall fall, when he hath been lord of poor men.
10.11: For he said in his heart, God hath forgotten; he hath turned away his face, that he see not into the end.
10.12: Lord God, rise thou up, and thine hand be enhanced; forget thou not poor men.
10.13: For what thing stirred the wicked man God to wrath? for he said in his heart, God shall not seek.
10.14: Thou seest, for thou beholdest travail and sorrow; that thou take them into thine hands. The poor man is left to thee; thou shalt be an helper to the fatherless and motherless.
10.15: All-break thou the arm of the sinner, and evil-willed; his sin shall be sought, and it shall not be found.
10.16: The Lord shall reign without end, and into the world of world; folks, ye shall perish from the land of him.
10.17: The Lord hath heard the desire of poor men; thine ear hath heard the making ready of their heart.
10.18: To deem for the motherless and meek; that a man presume no more to make himself great on earth.

11.1: To the victory, [[the psalm]] of David. I trust in the Lord; how say ye to my soul, Pass thou over into the hill, as a sparrow doeth?
11.2: For lo! sinners have bent a bow; they have made ready their arrows in an arrow case; that they shoot in darkness the rightful men in heart.
11.3: For they have destroyed, whom thou hast made perfect; but what did the rightful [[or rightwise]] man?
11.4: The Lord is in his holy temple; he is Lord, his seat is in heaven. His eyes behold on the poor man; his eyelids ask the sons of men.
11.5: The Lord asketh a just [[or right-wise]] man, and an unfaithful man; but he, that loveth wickedness, hateth his soul.
11.6: He shall rain snares upon sinners; fire, and brimstone, and the spirit of tempests be the part of the cup of them.
11.7: For the Lord is just [[or rightwise]], and loveth rightfulnesses [[or rightwise-ness]]; his cheer hath seen evenness, or equity.

12.1: To the victory, on the eighth, the song of David. Lord, make thou me safe, for the holy man failed; for truths be made little from the sons of men.
12.2: They spake vain things, each man to his neighbour; and they having guileful lips, spake in their heart, and with their heart.
12.3: The Lord destroy all guileful lips; and the great speaking tongue.
12.4: Which said, We shall magnify with our tongue, our lips be of us-selves; who else is our lord?
12.5: For the wretchedness of needy men, and for the wailing of poor men; now I shall rise up, saith the Lord. I shall set him in health; I shall do trustily in him.
12.6: The speeches of the Lord be chaste speeches; silver assayed by fire, proved from the earth, purged sevenfold.
12.7: Thou, Lord, shalt keep us; and thou shalt keep us from this gener-ation without end.
12.8: Wicked men go in compass; by thine highness thou hast multiplied the sons of men.

13.1: To the victory, [[the psalm]] of David. Lord, how long forgettest thou me, into the end? how long turnest thou away thy face from me?
13.2: How long shall I set counsel in my soul; sorrow in my heart by day? How long shall mine enemy be raised up on me?
13.3: My Lord God, behold thou, and hear thou me. Lighten thou mine eyes, lest any time I sleep in death;
13.4: lest any time mine enemy say, I had the mastery against him. They, that trouble me, shall have joy, if I shall be stirred;
13.5: but I hoped in thy mercy. Mine heart shall fully have joy in thine health;
13.6: I shall sing to the Lord, that giveth goods to me, and I shall say psalm to the name of the highest Lord.

14.1: To the victory, [[the psalm]] of David. The unwise man said in his heart, God is not. They be corrupt, and they be made abominable in their studies; none there is that doeth good, none is till to one.
14.2: The Lord beheld from heaven on the sons of men; that he see, if any is understanding, either seeking God.
14.3: All bowed away, altogether they be made unprofitable; none is that doeth good, none is till to one. The throat of them is an open sepulchre, they did guilefully with their tongues; the venom of snakes is under their lips. Whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness; their feet be swift to shed out blood. Sorrow and cursed-ness is in the ways of them, and they knew not the way of peace; the dread of God is not before their eyes.
14.4: Whether all men that work wicked-ness shall not know; that devour my people, as meat of bread? They called not the Lord;
14.5: they trembled there for dread, where was no dread; for the Lord is in a rightful [[or rightwise]] generation.
14.6: Thou hast shamed the counsel of a poor man; for the Lord is his hope.
14.7: Who shall give from Zion health to Israel? When the Lord hath turned away the captivity of his people; Jacob shall fully be joyful or shall full out joy, and Israel shall be glad.

15.1: The psalm of David. Lord, who shall dwell in thy tabernacle; either who shall rest in thine holy hill?
15.2: He that entereth without wem; and worketh rightfulness [[or rightwise-ness]]. He that speaketh truth in his heart;
15.3: which did not guile in his tongue. Nor did evil to his neighbour; and took not reproof against his neighbours.
15.4: A wicked man is brought to nought in his sight; but he glorifieth them that dread the Lord. He that sweareth to his neighbour, and deceiveth him not;
15.5: which gave not his money to usury; and took not gifts upon the innocent. He, that doeth these things, shall not be moved without end.

16.1: Of the meek and simple, the psalm of David. Lord, keep thou me, for I have hoped in thee;
16.2: I said to the Lord, Thou art my God; for thou hast no need of my goods.
16.3: To the saints that be in the land of him; he made wonderful all my wills in them.
16.4: The sicknesses of them be multi-plied; afterward they hasted. I shall not gather together the conventicles, or small covents, of them of bloods; and I shall not be mindful of their names by my lips.
16.5: The Lord is [[the]] part of mine heritage, and of my passion; thou art, that shall restore mine heritage to me.
16.6: Cords felled to me in full clear things; for mine heritage is full clear to me.
16.7: I shall bless the Lord, that hath given understanding to me; furthermore and my reins have blamed me unto the night.
16.8: I saw before me ever[[more]] the Lord in my sight; for he is at the right half to me, that I be not moved.
16.9: For this thing mine heart was glad, and my tongue joyed fully; further-more and my flesh shall rest in hope.
16.10: For thou shalt not leave my soul in hell; neither thou shalt give thine holy man to see corruption.
16.11: Thou hast made known to me the ways of life; thou shalt [[full-]]fill me with gladness with thy cheer; delight-ings be in thy right half unto the end.

17.1: The prayer of David. Lord, hear thou my rightfulness; behold thou my prayer. Perceive thou with ears my prayer; not made in guileful lips.
17.2: My doom come forth of thy cheer; thine eyes see they equity.
17.3: Thou hast proved mine heart, and hast visited me in [[the]] night; thou hast examined, or assayed, me by fire, and wickedness is not found in me.
17.4: That my mouth speak not of the works of men; for the words of thy lips I have kept hard ways.
17.5: Make thou perfect my goings in thy paths; that my steps be not moved.
17.6: I cried, for thou, God, heardest me; bow down thy ear to me, and hear thou my words.
17.7: Make wonderful thy mercies; that makest safe them that hope in thee.
17.8: Keep thou me as the apple of thine eye; and from them that against-stand thy right hand. Cover thou me under the shadow of thy wings;
17.9: from the face of unpious men, that have tormented me. Mine enemies have encompassed my soul;
17.10: they have closed together their fatness; the mouth of them spake pride.
17.11: They casted me forth, and have en-compassed me now; they ordained to bow down their eyes into [[the]] earth.
17.12: They, as a lion made ready to his prey, have taken me; and as the whelp of a lion dwelling in hid places.
17.13: Lord, rise thou up, before come thou him, and deceive or overturn thou him; deliver thou my life from the unpious, deliver thou thy sword;
17.14: from the enemies of thine hand. Lord, part thou them from a few men of the land in the life of them; their womb is [[full-]]filled of thine hid things. They be [[full-]]filled with sons; and they left their remnants, either residue, to their little children.
17.15: But I in rightfulness [[or rightwise-ness]] shall appear to thy sight; I shall be [[ful]] filled, when thy glory shall appear.

18.1: To victory, the word of the Lord to David, which spake the words of this song, in the day in which the Lord delivered him from the hand of all his enemies, and from the hand of Saul; and he said: Lord, my strength, I shall love thee;
18.2: the Lord is my steadfastness, and my refuge, and my deliverer. My God is mine helper; and I shall hope in him. My defender, and the horn of mine health; and mine up-taker.
18.3: I shall praise, and inwardly call the Lord; and I shall be safe from mine enemies.
18.4: The sorrows of death encompassed me; and the strands [[or streams]] of wickedness have troubled me.
18.5: The sorrows of hell encompassed me; the snares of death before-occupied me.
18.6: In my tribulation I inwardly called the Lord; and I cried to my God. And he heard my voice from his holy temple; and my cry in his sight entered into his ears.
18.7: The earth was moved together, and trembled greatly; the foundaments of hills were troubled altogether, and moved together, for he was wroth to them.
18.8: Smoke went up in the ire [[or wrath]] of the Lord, and fire burnt out from his face; coals were kindled of him.
18.9: He bowed down heavens, and came down; and darkness was under his feet.
18.10: And he ascended [[or went]] on cherubim, and flew; he flew over the pens of winds.
18.11: And he setted [[or put]] darknesses his hiding place, his tabernacle in his compass; and dark water was in the clouds of the air.
18.12: Full clear clouds passed in his sight; hail and the coals of fire.
18.13: And the Lord thundered from heaven; and the Highest gave his voice, hail and coals of fire.
18.14: And he sent his arrows, and destroyed those men; he multiplied lightnings, and troubled those men.
18.15: And the wells of waters appeared; and the foundaments of the earth were showed. Lord, of thy blaming; of the breathing of the spirit of thine ire.
18.16: He sent from the highest place, and took me; and he took me from many waters.
18.17: He delivered me from my strongest enemies; and from them that hated me, for they were comforted on me.
18.18: They came before me in the day of my torment; and the Lord was made my defender.
18.19: And he led out me into breadth; he made me safe, for he would me.
18.20: And the Lord shall yield to me by my rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]]; and he shall yield to me by the cleanness of mine hands.
18.21: For I kept the ways of the Lord; and I did not go away unfaithfully from my God.
18.22: For all his dooms be in my sight; and I putted not away from me his rightfulnesses [[or rightwisenesses]].
18.23: And I shall be unwemmed with him; and I shall keep me from my wickedness.
18.24: And the Lord shall yield to me by my rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]]; and by the cleanness of mine hands in the sight of his eyes.
18.25: With the holy, thou shalt be holy; and with an innocent man, thou shalt be innocent.
18.26: And with a chosen man, thou shalt be chosen; and with a wayward man, thou shalt be wayward.
18.27: For thou shalt make safe a meek people; and thou shalt make meek the eyes of proud men.
18.28: For thou, Lord, lightenest my lantern; my God, lighten thou my darknesses.
18.29: For by thee I shall be delivered from temptation; and in my God I shall go over the wall.
18.30: My God, his way is undefouled; the speeches of the Lord be examined by fire; he is [[the]] defender of all men hoping in him.
18.31: For why, who is God, except the Lord? either who is God, except our God?
18.32: God that hath girded me with virtue; and hath set my way unwem-med.
18.33: Which made perfect my feet as the feet of harts; and ordaining me on high things.
18.34: Which teacheth mine hands to battle; and thou hast set mine arms as a brazen bow.
18.35: And thou hast given to me the covering of thine health; and thy right hand hath up-taken me. And thy chastising amended me into the end; and that chastising of thee shall teach me.
18.36: Thou alargedest my paces under me; and my steps be not made un-steadfast.
18.37: I shall pursue mine enemies, and I shall take them; and I shall not turn till they fail.
18.38: I shall all-break them, and they shall not be able to stand; they shall fall under my feet.
18.39: And thou hast girded me with virtue to battle; and thou hast overturned under me men rising against me.
18.40: And thou hast given mine enemies aback [[or back]] to me; and thou hast destroyed them that hated me.
18.41: They cried, and none there was that made them safe; they cried to the Lord, and he heard not them.
18.42: And I shall all-break them, as dust before the face of the wind; I shall do them away, as the clay of streets.
18.43: Thou shalt deliver me from [[the]] against-sayings of the people; thou shalt set me into the head of folks. The people, which I knew not, hath served me;
18.44: in the hearing of ear it obeyed to me. Alien sons lied down to me,
18.45: alien sons waxed eld; and went crooked from thy paths.
18.46: The Lord liveth, and my God be blessed; and the God of mine health be enhanced.
18.47: God, that givest vengeances to me, and makest subject peoples under me;
18.48: thou art my deliverer from my wrathful enemies. And thou shalt enhance me from them, that rise against me; thou shalt deliver me from a wicked man.
18.49: Therefore, Lord, I shall acknowl-edge to thee among nations; and I shall say psalm to thy name.
18.50: Magnifying the healths of his king; and doing mercy to his christ David, and to his seed till into the world.

19.1: To victory, the psalm of David. Heavens tell out the glory of God; and the firmament telleth the works of his hands.
19.2: The day telleth out to the day a word; and the night showeth know-ing to the night.
19.3: No languages be, neither words; of which the voices of them be not heard.
19.4: The sound of them went out into all earth; and the words of them into the ends of the world. In the sun he hath set his tabernacle;
19.5: and he as a spouse coming forth of his chamber. He fully joyed, as a giant, to run his way;
19.6: his going out was from [[the]] high-est heaven. And his going again was to the highest thereof; and none there is that hideth himself from his heat.
19.7: The law of the Lord is without wem, and converteth souls; the wit-nessing of the Lord is faithful, and giveth wisdom to little, either meek, children.
19.8: The rightfulnesses of the Lord be rightful, gladdening hearts; the com-mandment of the Lord is clear, en-lightening eyes.
19.9: The holy dread of the Lord dwelleth into the world of world; the dooms of the Lord be true, justified into themselves.
19.10: Desirable more than gold, and a stone much precious; and sweeter than honey and honeycomb.
19.11: Forsooth thy servant keepeth those [[or them]]; much yielding is in those dooms to be kept.
19.12: Who understandeth trespasses? make thou me clean from my privy sins;
19.13: and of alien sins spare thy servant. If those [[or they]] have not lordship of me, then I shall be undefouled of alien sins, or without wem; and I shall be cleansed of the most sin.
19.14: And the speeches of my mouth shall be such, that they please; and the thinking of mine heart is ever[[more]] in thy sight. Lord, mine helper; and mine again-buyer.

20.1: To victory, the psalm of David. The Lord hear thee in the day of tribulation; the name of God of Jacob defend thee.
20.2: Send he help to thee from the holy place; and from Zion defend he thee.
20.3: Be he mindful of all thy sacrifice; and thy burnt sacrifice be made fat.
20.4: Give he to thee after thine heart; and confirm he all thy counsel.
20.5: We shall be glad in thine health; and we shall be magnified in the name of our God. The Lord [[ful]] fill all thine askings;
20.6: now I have known, that the Lord hath made safe his christ. He shall hear him from his holy heaven; the health of his right hand is in powers.
20.7: These, that is, adversaries, trust in chariots, and these in horses; but we shall inwardly call in the name of our Lord God.
20.8: They be bound, and felled down; but we have risen, and be raised.
20.9: Lord, make thou safe the king; and hear thou us in the day in which we inwardly call thee.

21.1: To victory, the psalm of David. Lord, the king shall be glad in thy virtue; and he shall full out have joy greatly on thine health.
21.2: Thou hast given to him the desire of his heart; and thou hast not defrauded him of the will of his lips.
21.3: For thou hast before-come him in the blessings of sweetness; thou hast set [[or puttest]] on his head a crown of precious stone.
21.4: He asked of thee life, and thou gavest it to him; the length of days into the world, and into the world of world.
21.5: His glory is great in thine health; thou shalt put glory, and great fairness, on him.
21.6: For thou shalt give him into bless-ing into the world of world; thou shalt make him glad in joy with thy cheer.
21.7: For the king hopeth in the Lord; and in the mercy of the Highest he shall not be moved.
21.8: Thine hand be found to all thine enemies; thy right hand find all them that hate thee.
21.9: Thou shalt put them as a furnace of fire in the time of thy cheer; the Lord shall trouble them in his ire, and fire shall devour them.
21.10: Thou shalt lose the fruit of them from the earth; and the seed of them from the sons of men.
21.11: For they bowed evil against thee; they thought counsels, which they might not stablish.
21.12: For thou shalt put them aback; in thy remnants thou shalt make ready the cheer of them.
21.13: Lord, be thou enhanced in thy virtue; we shall sing, and say openly thy virtues.

22.1: To the overcomer, for the morrow-tide hind, the psalm of David. God, my God, behold thou on me, why hast thou forsaken me? the words of my trespasses be far from mine health.
22.2: My God, I shall cry by day, and thou shalt not hear; and by night, and not to unwisdom to me.
22.3: Forsooth thou, the praising of Israel, dwellest in holiness;
22.4: our fathers hoped in thee; they hoped, and thou deliveredest them.
22.5: They cried to thee, and they were made safe; they hoped in thee, and they were not shamed.
22.6: But I am a worm, and not a man; the shame of men, and the out-casting of the people.
22.7: All men seeing me scorned me; they spake with lips, and wagged the head, and said,
22.8: He hoped in the Lord, deliver he him; make he him safe, for he will or delights in him.
22.9: For thou it art that drewest me out of the womb, that art mine hope from the teats of my mother;
22.10: into thee I am cast forth from the womb. From the womb of my mother thou art my God;
22.11: depart thou not from me. For tribulation is next; for none there is that helpeth.
22.12: Many calves encompassed me; fat bulls besieged me.
22.13: They opened their mouth on me; as a lion ravishing and roaring.
22.14: I am poured out as water; and all my bones be scattered. Mine heart is made, as wax floating abroad [[or melting]]; in the midst of my womb.
22.15: My virtue dried as a tilestone, and my tongue cleaved to my cheeks; and thou hast brought forth me into the dust of death.
22.16: For many dogs encompassed me; the council of wicked men besieged me. They delved mine hands and my feet;
22.17: they numbered all my bones. Soothly they looked, and beheld me;
22.18: they parted my clothes to them-selves, and they sent lot on my cloth.
22.19: But thou, Lord, delay not thine help from me; behold thou to my defence.
22.20: God, deliver thou my life from sword; and deliver thou mine one alone from the hand, or power, of the dog.
22.21: Make thou me safe from the mouth of a lion; and my meekness from the horns of unicorns.
22.22: I shall tell thy name to my brethren; I shall praise thee in the midst of the church.
22.23: Ye that dread the Lord, praise him; all the seed of Jacob, glorify him. All the seed of Israel, dread him;
22.24: for he forsook not, neither despised the prayer of a poor man. Neither he turned away his face from me; and when I cried to him, he heard me.
22.25: My praising is with thee in a great church; I shall yield my vows in the sight of men dreading him.
22.26: Poor men shall eat, and shall be [[ful]] filled, and they shall praise the Lord, that seek him; the hearts of them shall live into the world of world.
22.27: All the ends of earth shall bethink; and shall be converted to the Lord. And all the meines of heathen men, shall worship in his sight.
22.28: For the realm is the Lord’s; and he shall be Lord of heathen men.
22.29: All the fat men of earth ate and worshipped; all men, that go down into earth, shall fall down in his sight. And my soul shall live to him;
22.30: and my seed shall serve him. A generation to coming shall be told to the Lord;
22.31: and heavens shall tell his rightful-ness [[or rightwiseness]] to the people that shall be born, whom the Lord made.

23.1: The psalm of David. The Lord governeth me, and nothing shall fail to me;
23.2: in the place of pasture there he hath set me. He nourished me on the water of refreshing;
23.3: he converted my soul. He led me forth on the paths of rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]]; for his name.
23.4: For why though I shall go in the midst of shadow of death; I shall not dread evils, for thou art with me. Thy rod and thy staff; those have comforted me.
23.5: Thou hast made ready a board in my sight; against them that trouble me. Thou hast made fat mine head with oil; and my cup, that filleth greatly, is full clear.
23.6: And thy mercy shall follow me; in all the days of my life. And that I dwell in the house of the Lord; into the length of days.

24.1: The psalm of David. The earth and the fullness thereof is the Lord’s; the world, and all that dwell therein.
24.2: For he founded it on the seas; and made it ready on floods.
24.3: Who shall ascend or go up into the hill of the Lord; either who shall stand in the holy place of him?
24.4: The innocent in hands, that is, in works, and in clean heart; which took not his soul in vain, neither swore in guile to his neighbour.
24.5: He shall take blessing of the Lord; and mercy of God his health.
24.6: This is the generation of men seeking him; of men seeking the face of God of Jacob.
24.7: Ye princes, take up your gates, and ye everlasting gates, be ye raised; and the king of glory shall enter.
24.8: Who is this king of glory? the Lord strong and mighty, the Lord mighty in battle.
24.9: Ye princes, take up your gates, and ye everlasting gates, be ye raised; and the king of glory shall enter.
24.10: Who is this king of glory? the Lord of virtues or the Lord of hosts, he is the king of glory.

25.1: The song of David. Lord, to thee I have raised my soul;
25.2: my God, I trust in thee, be I not ashamed. Neither mine enemies scorn me;
25.3: for all men that suffer thee shall not be shamed. All men doing wicked things superfluously; be they shamed.
25.4: Lord, show thou thy ways to me; and teach thou me thy paths.
25.5: Dress thou me in thy truth, and teach thou me, for thou art God, my saviour; and I suffered thee all day.
25.6: Lord, have thou mind of thy merciful doings; and of thy mercies that be from the world.
25.7: Have thou not mind on the tres-passes of my youth; and on mine unknowings. Thou, Lord, have mind on me by thy mercy; for thy goodness.
25.8: The Lord is sweet and rightful; for this cause he shall give a law to men trespassing in the way.
25.9: He shall dress meek men in doom; he shall teach mild men his ways.
25.10: All the ways of the Lord be mercy and truth; to men seeking his testament, and his witnessings.
25.11: Lord, for thy name, thou shalt do mercy to my sin; for it is much.
25.12: Who is a man, that dreadeth the Lord? he ordaineth to him a law in the way which he should choose.
25.13: His soul shall dwell in goods; and his seed shall inherit the land.
25.14: The Lord is a firmness to men dreading him; and his testament is, that it be showed to them.
25.15: Mine eyes be ever[[more]] toward the Lord; for he shall pull away [[or pull up]] my feet from the snare.
25.16: Behold thou to me, and have thou mercy on me; for I am one alone and poor.
25.17: The tribulations of mine heart be multiplied; deliver thou me of my needs.
25.18: See thou my meekness and my travail; and forgive thou all my tres-passes.
25.19: Behold thou mine enemies, for they be multiplied; and they hate me by wicked hatred.
25.20: Keep thou my soul, and deliver me; be I not ashamed, for I hoped in thee.
25.21: Innocent men and rightful cleaved to me; for I suffered thee.
25.22: God, deliver thou Israel; from all his tribulations.

26.1: [[The psalm of David.]] Lord, deem thou me, for I entered in mine inno-cence; and I hoping in the Lord, shall not be made unsteadfast.
26.2: Lord, prove thou me, and assay me; burn thou my reins, and mine heart.
26.3: For why thy mercy is before mine eyes; and I pleased in thy truth.
26.4: I sat not with the counsel of vanity; and I shall not enter with men doing wicked things.
26.5: I hated the church of evil men; and I shall not sit with wicked men.
26.6: I shall wash mine hands among innocents; and, Lord, I shall compass thine altar.
26.7: That I hear the voice of praising; and that I tell out all thy marvels.
26.8: Lord, I have loved the fairness of thine house; and the place of the dwelling of thy glory.
26.9: God, lose thou not my soul with unfaithful men; and my life with men of bloods.
26.10: In whose hands wickednesses be; the right hand of them is full-filled with gifts.
26.11: But I entered in mine innocence; again-buy thou me, and have mercy on me.
26.12: My foot stood in rightfulness; Lord, I shall bless thee in churches.

27.1: The holy prayer of David. The Lord is my lightening, and mine health; whom shall I dread? The Lord is defender of my life; for whom shall I tremble [[or quake]]?
27.2: The while noisome men nigh on me; for to eat my fleshes. Mine enemies, that troubled me; they were made sick and felled [[or fell]] down.
27.3: Though castles [[or tents]] stand together against me; mine heart shall not dread. Though battle riseth against me; in this thing I shall have hope.
27.4: I asked of the Lord one thing; I shall seek this thing; that I dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life. That I see the will of the Lord; and that I visit his temple.
27.5: For he hid me in his tabernacle in the day of evils; he defended me in the hid place of his tabernacle. He enhanced me in a stone;
27.6: and now he enhanced mine head over mine enemies. I compassed, and offered in his tabernacle a sacrifice of crying [[out]]; I shall sing, and I shall say psalm to the Lord.
27.7: Lord, hear thou my voice, by which I cried to thee; have thou mercy on me, and hear me.
27.8: Mine heart said to thee, My face sought thee; Lord, I shall seek again thy face.
27.9: Turn thou not away thy face from me; bow thou not away in wrath from thy servant. Lord, be thou mine helper, forsake thou not me; and, God, mine health, despise thou not me.
27.10: For my father and my mother have forsaken me; but the Lord hath taken me up.
27.11: Lord, set thou a law to me in thy way; and dress thou me in a rightful [[or right]] path, for mine enemies.
27.12: Betake thou not me into the souls of them, that trouble me; for wicked witnesses have risen against me, and wickedness lied to itself.
27.13: I believe to see the goods of the Lord; in the land of living men.
27.14: Abide thou the Lord, do thou manly; and thine heart be comforted, and suffer thou for the Lord.

28.1: To David. [[The psalm to this David.]] Lord, I shall cry to thee; my God, be thou not still from me, be thou not still any time from me; and I shall be made like to them, that go down into the pit.
28.2: Lord, hear thou the voice of my beseeching, while I pray to thee; while I raise mine hands toward thine holy temple.
28.3: Betake thou not me together with sinners; and lose thou not me with them that work wickedness. Which speak peace to their neighbours; but evils be in their hearts.
28.4: Give thou to them after the works of them; and after the wickedness of their findings. Give thou to them after the works of their hands; yield thou their yielding to them.
28.5: For they understood not the works of the Lord, and by the works of his hands thou shalt destroy them; and thou shalt not build them.
28.6: Blessed be the Lord; for he heard the voice of my beseeching.
28.7: The Lord is mine helper and my defender; and mine heart hoped in him, and I am helped. And my flesh flowered again; and of my will I shall acknowledge to him.
28.8: The Lord is the strength of his people; and he is the defender of the savings of his christ.
28.9: Lord, make thou safe thy people, and bless thou thine heritage; and rule thou them, and enhance thou them till into without end.

29.1: The psalm of David. Ye sons of God, bring to the Lord; bring ye to the Lord, the sons of rams. Bring ye to the Lord glory and honour;
29.2: bring ye to the Lord glory to his name; praise ye the Lord in his holy large place.
29.3: The voice of the Lord on waters, God of majesty thundered; the Lord on many waters.
29.4: The voice of the Lord in virtue; the voice of the Lord in great doing.
29.5: The voice of the Lord breaking cedars; and the Lord shall break the cedars of Lebanon.
29.6: And he shall all-break them to dust, as a calf of the Lebanon; and the darling was as the son of an unicorn.
29.7: The voice of the Lord parting the flames of fire;
29.8: the voice of the Lord shaking desert; and the Lord shall stir altogether the desert of Kadesh.
29.9: The voice of the Lord making ready harts to calve, and he shall show thick things; and in his temple all men shall say glory.
29.10: The Lord maketh to inhabit the great flood; and the Lord shall sit King without end.
29.11: The Lord shall give virtue to his people; the Lord shall bless his people in peace.

30.1: The psalm of [[the]] song, for the hallowing of the house of David. Lord, I shall enhance thee, for thou hast up-taken me; and thou delighted-est not mine enemies on me.
30.2: My Lord God, I cried to thee; and thou madest me whole.
30.3: Lord, thou leddest out my soul from hell; thou savedest me from them that go down into the pit.
30.4: Ye saints of the Lord, sing to the Lord; and acknowledge ye to the mind of his holiness.
30.5: For ire is in his indignation; and life is in his will. Weeping shall dwell at eventide; and gladness at the morrowtide.
30.6: Forsooth I said in my plenty; I shall not be moved without end.
30.7: Lord, in thy will; thou hast given virtue to my fairness. Thou turnedest away thy face from me; and I am made troubled.
30.8: Lord, I shall cry to thee; and I shall pray to my God.
30.9: What profit is in my blood; while I go down into corruption? Whether dust shall acknowledge to thee; either it shall tell of thy truth?
30.10: The Lord heard, and had mercy on me; the Lord is made mine helper.
30.11: Thou hast turned my wailing into joy to me; thou hast rent my sack-cloth, and hast encompassed me with gladness.
30.12: That my glory sing to thee, and I be not compunct; my Lord God, I shall acknowledge to thee without end.

31.1: To victory, the psalm of David. Lord, I have hoped in thee, be I not shamed without end; deliver thou me in thy rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]].
31.2: Bow down thine ear to me; haste thou to deliver me. Be thou to me into God a defender, and into an house of refuge; that thou make me safe.
31.3: For thou art my strength and my refuge; and for thy name, thou shalt lead me forth, and shalt nourish me.
31.4: Thou shalt lead me out of the snare, which they hid to me; for thou art my defender.
31.5: I betake my spirit into thine hands; Lord God of truth, thou hast again-bought me.
31.6: Thou hatest them that keep vanities superfluously. Forsooth I hoped in the Lord;
31.7: I shall have fully joy, and shall be glad in thy mercy. For thou beheldest my meekness; thou savedest my life from needs.
31.8: And thou enclosedest not me altogether within the hands of the enemy; thou hast set my feet in a large place.
31.9: Lord, have thou mercy on me, for I am troubled; mine eye is troubled in ire, my soul and my womb also.
31.10: For why my life failed in sorrow; and my years in wailings. My virtue is made feeble in poverty; and my bones be troubled.
31.11: Over all mine enemies I am made a shame, [[and]] greatly to my neighbours; and dread to my known. They that saw me withoutforth, fled from me;
31.12: I am given to forgetting, as a dead man from the heart. I am made as a forlorn vessel;
31.13: for I heard despising of many men dwelling in compass. In that thing while they came together against me; they counselled to take my life.
31.14: But, Lord, I hoped in thee; I said, Thou art my God;
31.15: my times be in thine hands. Deliver thou me from the hands of mine enemies; and from them that pursue me.
31.16: Make thou clear thy face on thy servant; Lord, make thou me safe in thy mercy;
31.17: be I not shamed, for I inwardly called thee. Unpious men be ashamed, and be they led forth into hell;
31.18: guileful lips be made dumb. That speak wickedness against a just [[or rightwise]] man; in pride, and in mis-using or in abusing.
31.19: Lord, the multitude of thy sweet-ness is full great; which thou hast hid to men dreading thee. Thou hast made a perfect thing to them that hope in thee; in the sight of the sons of men.
31.20: Thou shalt hide them in the private of thy face; from [[the]] troubling of men. Thou shalt defend them in thy tabernacle; from [[the]] against-saying of tongues.
31.21: Blessed be the Lord; for he hath made wonderful his mercy to me in a strengthened city.
31.22: Forsooth I said in the out-passing of my soul; I am cast out from the face of thine eyes. Therefore thou heardest the voice of my prayer; while I cried to thee.
31.23: All ye holy men of the Lord, love him; for the Lord shall seek truth, and he shall yield plenteously to them that do pride.
31.24: All ye that hope in the Lord, do ye manly; and your heart be comforted.

32.1: Learning to David. [[The under-standing of David.]] Blessed be they, whose wickedness be forgiven; and whose sins be covered.
32.2: Blessed is the man, to whom the Lord areckoned not sin; neither guile is in his spirit.
32.3: For I was still, my bones waxed eld; while I cried all day.
32.4: For by day and night thine hand was made grievous on me; I am turned in my wretchedness, while the thorn is set in.
32.5: I made my sin known to thee; and I hid not my unrightfulness. I said, I shall acknowledge against me mine unrightfulness to the Lord; and thou hast forgiven the wickedness of my sin.
32.6: For this thing each holy man shall pray to thee; in covenable time. Nevertheless in the great flood of many waters; they shall not nigh to thee.
32.7: Thou art my refuge from tribulation, that encompassed me; thou, my fully joying [[or full out joy]], deliver me from them that encompass me.
32.8: I shall give understanding to thee, and I shall teach thee; in this way in which thou shalt go, I shall make steadfast mine eyes on thee.
32.9: Do not ye be made as an horse and mule; to which is none under-standing. Lord, constrain thou the cheeks of them with a barnacle and bridle; that they nigh not to thee.
32.10: Many beatings be of the sinner; but mercy shall encompass him that hopeth in the Lord.
32.11: Ye just [[or rightwise]] men, be glad, and make fully joy in the Lord; and all ye rightful of heart, have glory.

33.1: Ye just [[or rightwise]] men, have fully joy [[or full out joyeth]] in the Lord; praising altogether becometh rightful [[or right]] men.
33.2: Acknowledge ye to the Lord in an harp; sing ye to him in a psaltery of ten strings.
33.3: Sing ye to him a new song; say ye well psalm to him in crying [[out]].
33.4: For the word of the Lord is rightful [[or right]]; and all his works be in faithfulness.
33.5: He loveth mercy and doom; the earth is full of the mercy of the Lord.
33.6: Heavens be made steadfast by the word of the Lord; and all the virtue of those [[or them]] by the spirit of his mouth.
33.7: And he gathered together the waters of the sea as in a bouget or a bottle; and he setteth deep waters in treasures.
33.8: All earth dread the Lord; soothly all men inhabiting the world be moved of him.
33.9: For he said, and things were made; he commanded, and things were made of nought.
33.10: The Lord destroyeth the counsels of folks, forsooth he reproveth the thoughts of peoples; and he reproveth the counsels of princes.
33.11: But the counsel of the Lord dwelleth without end; the thoughts of his heart dwell in generation and into generation.
33.12: Blessed is the folk, whose Lord is his God; the people which he chose into heritage to himself.
33.13: The Lord beheld from heaven; he saw all the sons of men.
33.14: From his dwelling place made ready before; he beheld on all men, that inhabit the earth.
33.15: Which made singularly, either each by himself, the souls of them; which understandeth all the works of them.
33.16: A king is not saved by much virtue, that is, strength; and a giant shall not be saved in the muchliness of his virtue.
33.17: An horse is false to health; for-sooth he shall not be saved in the abundance, either plenty, of his virtue.
33.18: Lo! the eyes of the Lord be on men dreading him; and in them that hope in his mercy.
33.19: That he deliver their souls from death; and feed them in hunger.
33.20: Our soul suffereth the Lord, that is, abideth patiently his will; for he is our helper and defender.
33.21: For our heart shall be glad in him; and we shall have hope in his holy name.
33.22: Lord, thy mercy be made on us; as we hoped in thee.

34.1: To David, when he changed his mouth, or his word, before Abimelech, and he drove out David, and he went forth. [[The psalm of David, when he changed his cheer before Abimelech, and he let him go, and he went away.]] I shall bless the Lord in all time; ever[[more]] his praising be in my mouth.
34.2: My soul shall be praised in the Lord; mild men hear, and be glad.
34.3: Magnify ye the Lord with me; and enhance we his name into itself.
34.4: I sought the Lord, and he heard me; and he delivered me from all my tribulations.
34.5: Nigh ye to him, and be ye lighten-ed; and your faces shall not be shamed.
34.6: This poor man cried, and the Lord heard him; and saved him from all his tribulations.
34.7: The angel of the Lord sendeth in the compass of men dreading him; and he shall deliver them.
34.8: Taste ye, and see, for the Lord is sweet; blessed is the man, that hopeth in him.
34.9: All ye holy men of the Lord, dread ye him; for no neediness is to men dreading him.
34.10: Rich men were needy, and were hungry; but men that seek the Lord shall not fail of all good.
34.11: Come, ye sons, hear ye me; I shall teach you the dread of the Lord.
34.12: Who is the man, that willeth or desireth life; that loveth to see good days?
34.13: Forbid thy tongue from evil; and thy lips speak not guile.
34.14: Turn thou away from evil, and do good; seek thou peace, and perfectly pursue thou it.
34.15: The eyes of the Lord be on just [[or rightwise]] men; and his ears be to their prayers.
34.16: But the cheer of the Lord is on men doing evils; that he lose the mind the memory of them from [[the]] earth.
34.17: Just [[or rightwise]] men cried, and the Lord heard them; and delivered them from all their tribulations.
34.18: The Lord is nigh [[to]] them that be of troubled heart; and he shall save meek men in spirit.
34.19: Many tribulations be of just [[or rightwise]] men; and the Lord shall deliver them from all these [[or them]].
34.20: The Lord keepeth all the bones of them; one of those [[or them]] shall not be broken.
34.21: The death of sinners is worst; and they that hate a just [[or rightwise]] man shall trespass.
34.22: The Lord shall again-buy the souls of his servants; and all, that hope in him, shall not trespass.

35.1: To David. [[The psalm of David.]] Lord, deem thou them, that annoy me; overcome thou them, that fight against me.
35.2: Take thou armours and shield; and rise up into help to me.
35.3: Hold out the sword, and close altogether the way against them that pursue me; say thou to my soul, I am thine health.
35.4: They that seek my life; be shamed, and ashamed. They that think evils to me; be turned away backward, and be they shamed.
35.5: Be they made as dust before the face of the wind; and the angel of the Lord make them strait.
35.6: Their way be made darkness, and sliderness; and the angel of the Lord pursue them.
35.7: For without cause they hid to me the death of their snare; in vain they despised my soul.
35.8: The snare which he knoweth not come to him, and the taking which he hid take him; and fall he into the snare in that thing.
35.9: But my soul shall fully have joy in the Lord; and shall delight on his health.
35.10: All my bones shall say, Lord, who is like thee? Thou deliverest a poor man from the hand of his stronger; a needy man and poor from them that diversely ravish him.
35.11: Wicked witnesses rising asked me things, which I knew not.
35.12: They yielded to me evils for goods; barrenness to my soul.
35.13: But when they were dis-easeful to me; I was clothed in an hair-shirt. I meeked my soul in fasting; and my prayer shall be turned into my bosom.
35.14: I pleased so as our neighbour, as our brother; I was made meek, so as mourning and sorrowful.
35.15: And they were glad, and came together against me; torments were gathered on me, and I knew it not. They were scattered, and not compunct;
35.16: they tempted me, they scorned me with mocking, they gnashed on me with their teeth.
35.17: Lord, when thou shalt behold, restore thou my soul from the wicked-ness of them; mine one alone from lions.
35.18: I shall acknowledge to thee in a great church; I shall praise thee in a firm people.
35.19: They that be adversaries wickedly to me, have not joy on me; that hate me without cause, and beckon with eyes.
35.20: For soothly they spake not peace-ably to me; and they speaking in wrath-fulness of [[the]] earth, thought guiles.
35.21: And they made large their mouth on me; they said, Well, well! our eyes have seen.
35.22: Lord, thou hast seen, be thou not still; Lord, depart thou not from me.
35.23: Rise up, and give attention to my doom; my God and my Lord, behold into my cause.
35.24: My Lord God, deem thou me by thy rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]]; and have they not joy on me.
35.25: Say they not in their hearts, Well, well, to our soul; neither say they, We shall devour him.
35.26: Shame they, and dread they together; that joy for mine evils. Be they clothed with shame and dread; that speak evil things on me.
35.27: Have they full joy, and be they glad, that will or desire my rightful-ness [[or rightwiseness]]; and say they ever[[more]], The Lord be magnified, which desire the peace of his servant.
35.28: And my tongue shall bethink thy rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]]; all day thy praising.

36.1: To victory, to David [[or the psalm of David]], the servant of the Lord. The unjust man said, that he trespass in himself; the dread of God is not before his eyes.
36.2: For he did guilefully in the sight of God; that his wickedness be found to be hatred.
36.3: The words of his mouth be wickedness and guile; he would not understand to do well.
36.4: He thought wickedness in his bed; he stood nigh all ways not good; forsooth he hated not malice.
36.5: Lord, thy mercy is in heaven; and thy truth is unto [[the]] clouds.
36.6: Thy rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]] is as the hills of God; thy dooms be as much depth of waters. Lord, thou shalt save men and beasts;
36.7: as thou, God, hast multiplied thy mercy. But the sons of men shall hope in the covering of thy wings.
36.8: They shall be filled greatly of the plenty of thine house; and thou shalt give drink to them of the stiff stream of thy liking [[or thy delight]].
36.9: For the well of life is with thee; and in thy light we shall see light.
36.10: Lord, set forth thy mercy to them that know thee; and thy rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]] to them that be of rightful [[or right]] heart.
36.11: The foot of pride come not to me; and the hand of the sinner move me not.
36.12: There they have fallen down, that work wickedness; they be cast out, and might not stand.

37.1: To David. [[The psalm of David.]] Do not thou pursue [[or follow]] wicked men; neither love thou men doing wickedness.
37.2: For they shall wax dry swiftly as hay; and they shall fall down soon as the worts of herbs.
37.3: Hope thou in the Lord, and do thou goodness; and inhabit thou the land, and thou shalt be fed with his riches.
37.4: Delight thou in the Lord; and he shall give to thee the askings of thine heart.
37.5: Show thy way to the Lord; and hope in him, and he shall do.
37.6: And he shall lead out thy rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]] as light, and thy doom as midday;
37.7: be thou subject to the Lord, and pray thou him. Do not thou pursue [[or follow]] him, that hath prosperity in his way; nor a man doing unright-fulness.
37.8: Cease thou of ire, and forsake strong vengeance; do not thou pursue [[or follow]], that thou do wickedly.
37.9: For they, that do wickedly, shall be destroyed; but they that suffer the Lord, shall inherit the land.
37.10: And yet a little, and a sinner shall not be; and thou shalt seek his place, and thou shalt not find it.
37.11: But mild men shall inherit the land; and shall delight in the multitude of peace.
37.12: A sinner shall ambush the rightful [[or rightwise]] man; and he shall gnash with his teeth on him.
37.13: But the Lord shall scorn the sinner; for he beholdeth that his day cometh.
37.14: Sinners have drawn out sword; they bent their bow. To deceive a poor man and needy; to strangle rightful [[or right]] men of heart.
37.15: Their sword enter into the heart of themselves; and their bow be broken.
37.16: Better is a little thing to a just [[or rightwise]] man; than many riches of sinners.
37.17: For the arms of sinners shall be all-broken; but the Lord confirmeth just [[or rightwise]] men.
37.18: The Lord knoweth the days of [[the]] unwemmed; and their heritage shall be without end.
37.19: They shall not be shamed in the evil time, and they shall be [[ful]] filled in the days of hunger;
37.20: for sinners shall perish. Forsooth anon as the enemies of the Lord be honoured, and enhanced; they failing shall fail as smoke.
37.21: A sinner shall borrow, and shall not pay back; but a just [[or rightwise]] man hath mercy, and shall give.
37.22: For they that bless the Lord shall inherit the land; but they that curse him shall perish.
37.23: The goings of a man shall be dressed with the Lord; and he shall delight in his way.
37.24: When he falleth, he shall not be hurtled or hurled down; for the Lord undersetteth his hand.
37.25: I was younger, and soothly I waxed eld; and I saw not a just [[or rightwise]] man forsaken, neither his seed seeking bread.
37.26: All day he hath mercy, and lendeth; and his seed shall be in blessing.
37.27: Bow thou away from evil, and do good; and dwell thou into the world of world.
37.28: For the Lord loveth doom, and shall not forsake his saints; they shall be kept without end. Unjust men shall be punished; and the seed of wicked men shall perish.
37.29: But just [[or rightwise]] men shall inherit the land; and shall inhabit thereon into the world of world.
37.30: The mouth of a just [[or rightwise]] man shall bethink wisdom; and his tongue shall speak doom.
37.31: The law of his God is in his heart; and his steps shall not be deceived.
37.32: A sinner beholdeth a just [[or right-wise]] man; and seeketh to slay him.
37.33: But the Lord shall not forsake him in his hands; neither he shall condemn him, when it shall be deemed against him.
37.34: Abide thou the Lord, and keep thou his way, and he shall enhance thee, that by heritage thou take the land; when sinners shall perish, thou shalt see.
37.35: I saw the wicked man enhanced above; and raised up as the cedars of Lebanon.
37.36: And I passed by, and lo! he was not there; I sought him, and his place was not found.
37.37: Keep thou innocence, and see equity; for those [[or they]] be relics or remnants to a peaceable man.
37.38: Forsooth unjust men shall perish; the remnants or relics of wicked men shall perish altogether.
37.39: But the health of just [[or rightwise]] men is of the Lord; and he is their defender in the time of tribulation.
37.40: And the Lord shall help them, and shall make them free, and he shall deliver them from sinners; and he shall save them, for they hoped in him.

38.1: The psalm of David, to bethink on the sabbath. Lord, reprove thou not me in thy strong vengeance; neither chastise thou me in thine ire.
38.2: For thine arrows be fixed in me; and thou hast made steadfast thine hand on me.
38.3: None health is in my flesh from the face of thine ire; no peace is to my bones from the face of my sins.
38.4: For my wickednesses be gone over mine head; as an heavy burden, those [[or they]] be made heavy on me.
38.5: Mine healed wounds were rotten, and be broken; from the face of mine unwisdom.
38.6: I am made a wretch, and I am bowed down till into the end; all day I entered sorrowful.
38.7: For my loins be filled with scorn-ings; and health is not in my flesh.
38.8: I am tormented, and made low full greatly; I roared for the wailing of mine heart.
38.9: Lord, all my desire is before thee; and my wailing is not hid from thee.
38.10: Mine heart is troubled in me, my virtue forsook me; and the light of mine eyes, and it is not with me.
38.11: My friends and my neighbours nighed; and stood against me. And they that were beside me stood afar;
38.12: and they did violence, that sought my life. And they that sought evils to me, spake vanities; and thought guiles [[or treacheries]] all day.
38.13: But I, as a deaf man, heard not; and as a dumb man not opening his mouth.
38.14: And I am made as a man not hearing; and not having reprovings in his mouth.
38.15: For, Lord, I hoped in thee; my Lord God, thou shalt hear me.
38.16: For I said, Hear me, Lest any time mine enemies have joy on me; and the while my feet be moved/and while my feet were moved, they spake great things on me.
38.17: For I am ready to beatings; and my sorrow is ever[[more]] in my sight.
38.18: For I shall tell my wickedness; and I shall think for my sin.
38.19: But mine enemies live, and they be confirmed on me; and they be multiplied, that hate me wickedly.
38.20: They that yield evils for goods, backbited me; for I pursued [[or followed]] goodness.
38.21: My Lord God, forsake thou not me; go thou not away from me.
38.22: Lord God of mine health; behold thou into mine help.

39.1: For victory, to Jeduthun, the psalm of David. I said, I shall keep my ways; that I trespass not in my tongue. I setted [[or put]] keeping to my mouth; when a sinner stood against me.
39.2: I was dumb, and I was meeked full greatly, and was still, even from goods; and my sorrow was renewed.
39.3: Mine heart was hot within me; and fire shall burn out in my thinking. I spake in my tongue;
39.4: Lord, make thou mine end known to me. And the number of my days, what it is; that I know, what faileth to me.
39.5: Lo! thou hast set [[or put]] my days measurable; and my substance is as nought before thee. Nevertheless all vanity; each man living.
39.6: Nevertheless a man passeth in an image; but also he is troubled vainly. He treasureth; and he know not, to whom he shall gather those things.
39.7: And now which is mine abiding? whether not the Lord? and my substance is at thee.
39.8: Deliver thou me from all my wickednesses; thou hast given me as a shame to the unknowing.
39.9: I was dumb, and opened not my mouth; for thou hast made this happen,
39.10: remove thou thy wounds from me. From the strength of thine hand I failed in blamings;
39.11: for wickedness thou hast chastised [[a]] man. And thou madest his life to fail as a spider; nevertheless each man is troubled in vain.
39.12: Lord, hear thou my prayer, and my beseeching; perceive thou with ears my tears. Be thou not still, for I am a comeling with thee; and a pilgrim, as all my fathers.
39.13: Forgive thou to me, that I be refreshed, before that I go; and I shall no more be.

40.1: For victory, the psalm of David. I abiding abode the Lord; and he gave attention to me. And he heard my prayers;
40.2: and he led out me from the pit of wretchedness, and from the filth of dregs. And he ordained my feet on a stone; and he dressed my goings.
40.3: And he sent into my mouth a new song; a song to our God. Many men shall see, and dread; and shall hope in the Lord.
40.4: Blessed is the man, of whom the name of the Lord is his hope; and he beheld not into vanities, and into false vengeances.
40.5: My Lord God, thou hast made thy marvels many; and in thy thoughts none is, that is like thee toward us. I told and I spake; and they be multiplied above number.
40.6: Thou wouldest or desiredest not sacrifice and offering; but thou madest perfectly ears to me. Thou askedest not burnt sacrifice, and other sacrifice for sin;
40.7: then I said, Lo! I come. In the head of the book it is written of me,
40.8: that I should do thy will; my God, I would also to do it; and thy law in the midst of mine heart.
40.9: I told thy rightfulness [[or rightwise-ness]] in a great church; lo! I shall not refrain my lips, Lord, thou knewest.
40.10: I hid not thy rightfulness [[or right-wiseness]] in mine heart; I said thy truth and thine health. I hid not thy mercy, and thy truth, from a much council.
40.11: But thou, Lord, make not far thy merciful doings from me; thy mercy and truth ever[[more]] take me up.
40.12: For why evils, of which is no number, encompassed me; my wicked-nesses have taken me, and I might not, that I should see. Those [[or They]] be multiplied above the hairs of mine head; and mine heart forsook me.
40.13: Lord, please it to thee, that thou deliver me; Lord, behold thou to help me.
40.14: Be they shamed, and ashamed together; that seek my life, to take away it. Be they turned aback, and be they shamed or ashamed; that will or desire evils to me.
40.15: Bear they their confusion anon; that say to me, Well! well! in scorn.
40.16: All men that seek thee, be fully joyful [[or full out joy]], and be glad in thee; and say they, that love thine health, The Lord be magnified ever-[[more]].
40.17: Forsooth I am a beggar and poor; the Lord is busy of me. Thou art mine helper and my defender; my God, tarry thou not.

41.1: For victory, the song of David. Blessed is he that understandeth of the needy man and poor; the Lord shall deliver him in the evil day.
41.2: The Lord keep him, and quicken him, and make him blessful in the land; and betake not him into the will of his enemies.
41.3: The Lord shall bear help to him on the bed of his sorrow; thou hast oft turned all his bedstraw in his sickness.
41.4: I said, Lord, have thou mercy on me; heal thou my soul, for I have sinned against thee.
41.5: Mine enemies said evils to me; When shall he die, and his name shall perish?
41.6: And if he entered for to see me, he spake vain things; his heart gathered wickedness to himself. He went with-outforth; and spake to the same thing or the same end.
41.7: All mine enemies backbited privily against me; against me they thought evils to me.
41.8: They ordained an evil word against me; Whether he that sleepeth, shall not lie to, that he rise again?
41.9: For why the man of my peace, in whom I hoped, he that ate my loaves; made great deceit on me.
41.10: But thou, Lord, have mercy on me, and raise me up again; and I shall yield to them.
41.11: In this thing I knew, that thou wouldest or delightest in me; for mine enemy shall not have joy on me.
41.12: Forsooth thou hast taken me up for mine innocence; and hast confirmed me in thy sight without end.
41.13: Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, from the world, and into the world; be it done, be it done.

42.1: To victory, [[by the understanding]], to the sons of Korah. As an hart desireth to the wells of waters; so thou, God, my soul desireth to thee.
42.2: My soul thirsted to God, the quick well or well of life; when shall I come, and appear before the face of God?
42.3: My tears were loaves to me day and night; while it is said to me each day, Where is thy God?
42.4: I bethought of these things, and I poured out in me my soul; for I shall pass into the place of the wonderful tabernacle, till to the house of God. In the voice of full out joying, and ac-knowledging; is the sound of the eater.
42.5: My soul, why art thou sorry; and why troublest thou me? Hope thou in God, for yet I shall acknowledge to him; he is the health of my cheer, and my God.
42.6: My soul is troubled within myself; therefore, God, I shall be mindful of thee from the land of Jordan, and from the little hill of Hermonites.
42.7: Depth calleth depth; in the voice of thy windows. All thine high things, and thy waves; passed over me.
42.8: The Lord sent his mercy in the day; and his song in the night. With me is the prayer to God of my life;
42.9: I shall say to God, Thou art mine up-taker. Why forgettest thou me; and why go I sorrowful, while the enemy tormenteth me?
42.10: While my bones be broken altogether; mine enemies, that trouble me, despised me. While they say to me, by all days; Where is thy God?
42.11: My soul, why art thou sorry; and why troublest thou me? Hope thou in God, for yet I shall acknowledge to him; he is the health of my cheer, and my God.

43.1: God, deem thou me, and separate thou my cause from a folk not holy; deliver thou me from a wicked man, and guileful [[or treacherous]].
43.2: For thou art God, my strength; why hast thou put me aback, and why go I sorrowful, while the enemy tormenteth me?
43.3: Send out thy light, and thy truth; those led me forth, and brought me into thine holy hill, and into thy tabernacles.
43.4: And I shall enter to the altar of God; to God, that gladdeth my youth. God, my God, I shall acknowledge to thee in an harp;
43.5: my soul, why art thou sorry, and why troublest thou me? Hope thou in God, for yet I shall acknowledge to him; that is the health of my cheer, and my God.

44.1: To victory, learning to the sons of Korah. God, we heard with our ears; our fathers told to us. The work, which thou wroughtest in the days of them; and in the old days.
44.2: Thine hand lost heathen men, and thou plantedest them; thou tormentedest peoples, and castedest them out.
44.3: For the children of Israel wielded the land not by their sword; and the arm of them saved not them. But thy right hand, and thine arm, and the lightening of thy cheer; for thou were pleased in them.
44.4: Thou art thyself, my king, and my God; that sendest healths to Jacob.
44.5: By thee we shall winnow our enemies with [[the]] horn; and in thy name we shall despise them, that rise against us.
44.6: For I shall not hope in my bow; and my sword shall not save me.
44.7: For thou hast saved us from men tormenting us; and thou hast shamed men hating us.
44.8: We shall be pleased in God all day; and in thy name we shall acknowledge to thee into the world.
44.9: But now thou hast put us aback, and hast shamed us; and thou, Lord, shalt not go out in our virtues.
44.10: Thou hast turned us away behind after our enemies; and they, that hated us, ravished diversely to themselves.
44.11: Thou hast given us as sheep of meats; and among heathen men thou hast scattered us.
44.12: Thou hast sold thy people without price; and multitude there was not in the exchangings of them.
44.13: Thou hast set [[or put]] us as a shame to our neighbours; mocking and scorn to them that be in our compass.
44.14: Thou hast set [[or put]] us into like-ness to heathen men; and wagging of the head among peoples.
44.15: All day my shame is against me; and the shame of my face covered me.
44.16: From the voice of [[the]] despiser, and evil speaker; from the face of the enemy, and [[the]] pursuer.
44.17: All these things came on us, and we have not forgotten thee; and we did not wickedly in thy testament.
44.18: And our heart went not away behind; and thou hast not bowed away our paths from thy way.
44.19: For thou hast made us low in the place of torment; and the shadow of death covered us.
44.20: If we forgat the name of our God; and if we held forth our hands to an alien God.
44.21: Whether God shall not seek these things? for he knoweth the hid things of heart.
44.22: For why we be slain all day for thee; we be deemed as sheep of slaying.
44.23: Lord, rise up, why sleepest thou? rise up, and put not us away into the end.
44.24: Why turnest thou away thy face? thou forgettest our poverty, and our tribulation.
44.25: For our life is made low in dust; our womb is glued together in the earth.
44.26: Lord, rise up thou, and help us; and again-buy us for thy name.

45.1: To the overcomer, for the lilies, the most loved song of learning of the sons of Korah. Mine heart hath told out a good word; I say my works to the king. My tongue is the pen of a writer; writing swiftly.
45.2: Christ, thou art fairer in shape than the sons of men; grace is spread abroad in thy lips; therefore God blessed thee without end.
45.3: Be thou gird with thy sword; on thy hip most mightily. Behold thou in thy shapeliness and thy fairness;
45.4: come thou forth with prosperity, and reign thou. For truth, and mildness, and rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]]; and thy right hand shall lead forth thee wonderfully.
45.5: Thy sharp arrows shall fall into the hearts of the enemies of the king; peoples shall be under thee.
45.6: God, thy seat is into the world of world; the rod of thy realm is a rod of right ruling, or of equity.
45.7: Thou lovedest rightfulness [[or right-wiseness]], and hatedest wickedness; therefore thou, God, thy God, anointed thee with the oil of gladness, more than thy fellows.
45.8: Myrrh, and gum, and cassia, of thy clothes, out of the ivory houses or the houses of ivory; of which the daughters of kings delighted thee.
45.9: A queen stood nigh on thy right side, in clothing overgilded; compassed with diversity.
45.10: Daughter, hear thou, and see, and bow down thine ear; and forget thy people, and the house of thy father.
45.11: And the king shall covet thy fair-ness; for he is thy Lord God, and they shall worship him.
45.12: And the daughters of Tyre in gifts; all the rich men of the people shall beseech thy cheer.
45.13: All the glory of that daughter of the king is within, adorned in golden hems;
45.14: she is clothed about with diversities. Virgins shall be brought to the king after her; her neighbouresses shall be brought to thee.
45.15: They shall be brought in gladness, and full out joying; they shall be brought into the temple of the king.
45.16: Sons be born to thee, for thy fathers; thou shalt ordain them princes on all earth.
45.17: Lord, they shall be mindful of thy name; in each generation, and into generation. Therefore peoples shall acknowledge to thee without end; and into the world of world.

46.1: To the overcomer, the song of the sons of Korah, for youths. Our God, thou art refuge, and virtue; helper in tribulations, that have found us greatly.
46.2: Therefore we shall not dread, while the earth shall be troubled; and the hills shall be borne over into the heart of the sea.
46.3: The waters of them sounded, and were troubled; hills were troubled altogether in the strength of him.
46.4: The fierceness of [[the]] flood maketh glad the city of God; the highest God hath hallowed his tabernacle.
46.5: God in the midst thereof shall not be moved; God shall help it early in the gray morrowtide.
46.6: Heathen men were troubled alto-gether, and realms were bowed down; God gave his voice, the earth was moved.
46.7: The Lord of virtues is with us; God of Jacob is our up-taker.
46.8: Come ye, and see the works of the Lord; which wonders he hath set on the earth.
46.9: He doing away battles till to the end of the land; shall all-bruise bow, and he shall break altogether armours [[or arms]], and he shall burn shields with fire.
46.10: Give ye attention, and see ye, that I am God; I shall be enhanced among heathen men; and I shall be enhanced in earth.
46.11: The Lord of virtues is with us; God of Jacob is our up-taker.

47.1: To victory, a psalm to the sons of Korah. All ye folks, make joy with hands; sing ye heartily to God in the voice of full out joying.
47.2: For the Lord is high and fearedful; a great king on all earth.
47.3: He made peoples subject to us; and heathen men under our feet.
47.4: He chose his heritage to us; the fairness of Jacob, whom he loved.
47.5: God ascended in hearty song; and the Lord in the voice of a trump.
47.6: Sing ye to our God, sing ye; sing ye to our king, sing ye.
47.7: For God is king of all earth; sing ye [[psalm]] wisely.
47.8: God shall reign on heathen men; God sitteth on his holy seat.
47.9: The princes of peoples be gath-ered together with God of Abraham; for the strong gods of earth be raised greatly.

48.1: The song of psalm, of the sons of Korah. The Lord is great, and worthy to be praised full much; in the city of our God, in the holy hill of him.
48.2: It is founded in the full out joying of all earth; the hill of Zion, the sides of the north, the city of the great king.
48.3: God shall be known in the houses thereof; when he shall take it.
48.4: For lo! the kings of earth were gathered together; they came into one place.
48.5: They seeing, so wondered; they were troubled, they were moved altogether,
48.6: trembling took them. There sorrows, as of a woman travailing of child;
48.7: in a great spirit thou shalt all-break the ships of Tarshish.
48.8: As we heard, so we saw, in the city of the Lord of virtues, in the city of our God; God hath founded that city without end.
48.9: God, we have received thy mercy; in the midst of thy temple.
48.10: After thy name, God, so thy praising is spread abroad into the ends of earth; thy right hand is full of rightwiseness.
48.11: The hill of Zion be glad, and the daughters of Judah be fully joyful [[or full out joy]]; for thy dooms, Lord.
48.12: Compass ye Zion, and embrace ye it; tell ye in the towers thereof.
48.13: Set ye your hearts in the virtue of him; and part ye the houses of him, that ye tell out in another generation.
48.14: For this is God, our God, into without end, and into the world of world; he shall govern us into worlds.

49.1: To victory, a psalm to the sons of Korah. All ye folks, hear these things; all ye that dwell in the world, perceive with ears.
49.2: All the sons of earth, and the sons of men; together the rich man, and the poor into one.
49.3: My mouth shall speak wisdom; and the thinking of mine heart shall speak prudence.
49.4: I shall bow down mine ear into a parable; I shall open my reason set forth in a psaltery.
