49.5: Why shall I dread in the evil day? the wickedness of mine heel shall encompass me.
49.6: Which trust in their own virtue; and have glory in the multitude of their riches.
49.7: A brother again-buyeth not, shall a man again-buy? and he shall not give to God his pleasing.
49.8: And he shall not be able to give the price of ransom for his soul; and he shall travail into without end,
49.9: and he shall live yet into the end. He shall not see perishing,
49.10: when he shall see wise men dying; the unwise man and the fool shall perish together. And they shall leave their riches to aliens;
49.11: and the sepulchres of them be the houses of them without end. The tabernacles of them be in generation and in generation; they called their names in their lands.
49.12: A man/Man, when he was in honour, understood not; he is compar-isoned to unwise beasts, and is made like to those [[or them]].
49.13: This way of them is cause of stumbling to them; and afterward they shall please altogether in their mouth.
49.14: As sheep they be put in hell; death shall gnaw them. And just men shall be lords of them in the morrow-tide; and the help of them shall wax eld [[or old]] in hell, for or from the glory of them.
49.15: Nevertheless God shall again-buy my soul from the power of hell; when he shall take me.
49.16: Dread thou not, when a man is made rich; and when the glory of his house is multiplied.
49.17: For when he shall die, he shall not take all things with him; and his glory shall not go down with him.
49.18: For his soul shall be blessed in his life; he shall acknowledge to thee, when thou hast done well to him.
49.19: He shall enter till into the gener-ations of his fathers; and till into with-out end he shall not see light.
49.20: A man/Man, when he was in honour, understood not; he is com-parisoned to unwise beasts, and is made like to those [[or them]].

50.1: The psalm of Asaph. God, the Lord of gods or God of gods, spake; and called the earth, from the rising of the sun till to the going down.
50.2: The shape of his fairness from Zion, God shall come openly;
50.3: our God, and he shall not be still. Fire shall burn on high in his sight; and a strong tempest in his compass.
50.4: He called heaven above; and the earth, to witness him deem his people.
50.5: Gather ye to him his saints; that ordain his testament above sacrifices.
50.6: And heavens shall show his rightwiseness or tell his rightfulness; for God is the judge.
50.7: My people, hear thou, and I shall speak to Israel; and I shall witness to thee, I am God, thy God.
50.8: I shall not reprove thee in thy sacrifices; and thy burnt sacrifices be ever[[more]] before me.
50.9: I shall not take calves of thine house; neither goat bucks of thy flocks.
50.10: For all the wild beasts of woods be mine; work beasts, and oxes [[or oxen]] in hills.
50.11: I have known all the volatiles of the firmament; and the fairness of the field is with me.
50.12: If I shall be hungry, I shall not say to thee; for the world and the fullness thereof is mine.
50.13: Whether I shall eat the flesh of bulls? either shall I drink the blood of goat bucks?
50.14: Offer thou to God the sacrifice of praising; and yield thine avows [[or vows]] to the highest God.
50.15: And inwardly call thou me in the day of tribulation; and I shall deliver thee, and thou shalt honour me.
50.16: But God said to the sinner, Why tellest thou out my rightfulnesses; and takest my testament by thy mouth?
50.17: Soothly thou hatedest lore, or discipline; and hast cast away my words behind thee.
50.18: If thou sawest a thief, thou rannest with him; and thou settedest thy part with adulterers.
50.19: Thy mouth was plenteous of malice; and thy tongue meddled together guiles [[or treacheries]].
50.20: Thou sitting spakest against thy brother, and thou settedest slander against the son of thy mother;
50.21: thou didest these things, and I was still. Thou guessedest wickedly, that I shall be like thee; I shall reprove thee, and I shall set against thy face.
50.22: Ye that forget God, understand these things; lest sometime he ravish, and none be that shall deliver.
50.23: The sacrifice of praising shall honour me; and there is the way, wherein I shall show to him the health of God.

51.1: To victory, the psalm of David, when Nathan the prophet came to him, when he entered to Bathsheba. God, have thou mercy on me; by thy great mercy. And by the muchliness of thy merciful doings; do thou away my wickedness.
51.2: Moreover wash thou me from my wickedness; and cleanse thou me from my sin.
51.3: For I acknowledge my wickedness; and my sin is ever[[more]] against me.
51.4: I have sinned to thee alone, and I have done evil before thee; that thou be justified in thy words, and overcome when thou art deemed.
51.5: For lo! I was conceived in wicked-nesses; and my mother conceived me in sins.
51.6: For lo! thou lovedest truth; thou hast showed to me the uncertain things, and privy things of thy wisdom.
51.7: Lord, sprinkle thou me with hyssop, and I shall be cleansed; wash thou me, and I shall be made white more than snow.
51.8: Give thou joy, and gladness to mine hearing; and bones made meek shall full out make joy.
51.9: Turn away thy face from my sins; and do away all my wickednesses.
51.10: God, make thou a clean heart in me; and make thou new a rightful spirit in my entrails.
51.11: Cast thou me not away from thy face; and take thou not away from me thine holy spirit.
51.12: Give thou to me the gladness of thine health; and confirm thou me with the principal spirit.
51.13: I shall teach wicked men thy ways; and unfaithful men shall be converted to thee.
51.14: God, the God of mine health, deliver thou me from bloods, or sins; and my tongue shall joyfully sing of thy rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]].
51.15: Lord, open thou my lips; and my mouth shall tell thy praising.
51.16: For if thou haddest would or desired sacrifice, I had given it; truly thou shalt not delight in burnt sacrifice.
51.17: A sacrifice to God is a spirit troubled, that is, sorry for sin; God, thou shalt not despise a contrite heart, and made meek.
51.18: Lord, do thou benignly in thy good will to Zion; that the walls of Jerusalem be builded.
51.19: Then thou shalt take pleasantly the sacrifice of rightfulness [[or rightwise-ness]], offerings, and burnt sacrifices; then they shall put calves on thine altar.

52.1: To victory, the psalm of David, when Doeg the Idumaean came, and told to Saul, and said to him, David came into the house of Ahimelech. What hast thou glory in malice; which art mighty in wickedness?
52.2: All day thy tongue thought unright-fulness; as a sharp razor thou hast done guile [[or treachery]].
52.3: Thou lovedest malice more than benignity; and wickedness more than to speak equity.
52.4: Thou lovedest all words of casting down; with a guileful [[or treacherous]] tongue.
52.5: Therefore God shall destroy thee into the end, he shall draw thee out by the root, and he shall make thee to pass away from thy tabernacle; and thy root from the land of living men.
52.6: Just [[or Rightwise]] men shall see, and shall dread; and they shall laugh on him,
52.7: and they shall say, Lo! the man that setted [[or put]] not God his helper. But he hoped in the multitude of his riches; and had mastery in his vanity.
52.8: Forsooth I, as a fruitful olive tree in the house of God; hoped in the mercy of God without end, and into the world of world.
52.9: I shall acknowledge to thee into the world, for thou hast done mercy to me; and I shall abide thy name, for it is good in the sight of thy saints.

53.1: To the overcomer, by the quire or choir, the learning of David. The unwise man said in his heart, God is not. They be corrupt, and made abom-inable in their wickednesses; none is that doeth good.
53.2: God beheld from heaven on the sons of men; that he see, if there is any understanding, either seeking God.
53.3: All bowed away, they be made unprofitable altogether; none is that doeth good, there is not till to one.
53.4: Whether all men, that work wicked-ness, shall not know; which devour my people, as the meat of bread? They called not God;
53.5: there they trembled for dread, where no dread was. For God hath scattered the bones of them, that please men; they be shamed, for God hath forsaken them.
53.6: Who shall give from Zion health to Israel? when the Lord hath turned the captivity of his people, Jacob shall full out make joy, and Israel shall be glad.

54.1: To victory, in organs, either in psalms, the learning of David, when Ziphims came, and said to Saul, Whether David is not hid at us? God, in thy name, make thou me safe; and in thy virtue, deem thou me.
54.2: God, hear thou my prayer; with ears perceive thou the words of my mouth.
54.3: For aliens have risen against me, and strong men sought my life; and they setted not God before their sight.
54.4: For lo! God helpeth me; and the Lord is the up-taker of my soul.
54.5: Turn thou away evils to mine enemies; and lose thou them in thy truth.
54.6: Willfully I shall sacrifice to thee; and, Lord, I shall acknowledge to thy name, for it is good.
54.7: For thou deliveredest me from all tribulation; and mine eye despised on mine enemies.

55.1: To victory, in organs, the learning of David. God, hear thou my prayer, and despise thou not my beseeching;
55.2: give thou attention to me, and hear thou me. I am sorrowful in mine exercising;
55.3: and I am disturbed of the face of the enemy, and of the tribulation of the sinner. For they bowed wicked-nesses into me; and in ire they were dis-easeful to me.
55.4: Mine heart was troubled in me; and the dread of death felled on me.
55.5: Dread and trembling came on me; and darknesses covered me.
55.6: And I said, Who shall give to me feathers, as of a culver; and I shall fly, and shall take rest?
55.7: Lo! I went far away, and fled; and I dwelled in wilderness.
55.8: I abode him, that made me safe from the littleness, either dread, of spirit; and from tempest.
55.9: Lord, cast thou down, [[and]] part thou the tongues of them; for I saw wickedness and against-saying in the city.
55.10: By day and night wickedness shall encompass it on the walls thereof; and travail and unrightfulness be in the midst of them.
55.11: And usury and guile [[or treachery]] failed not; from the streets thereof.
55.12: For if mine enemy had cursed me; soothly I had suffered. And if he, that hated me, had spoken great things on me; in hap I had hid me from him.
55.13: But thou art a man of one will; my leader, and my known.
55.14: Which tookest together sweet meats and fellowship with me; we went with consent in the house of God.
55.15: Death come on them; and go they down quick into hell. For way-wardnesses be in the dwelling places of them; in the midst of them.
55.16: But I cried to thee, Lord; and the Lord saved me.
55.17: In the eventide, and [[the]] morrow-tide, and in midday, I shall tell, and show; and he shall hear my voice.
55.18: He shall again-buy my soul in peace from them, that nigh to me; for among many they were with me.
55.19: God shall hear; and he that is before the worlds shall make them low. For changing is not to them, and they dreaded not God;
55.20: he holdeth forth his hand in yielding. They defouled his testament,
55.21: the cheers thereof were parted from ire; and his heart nighed. The words thereof were softer than oil; and they be darts.
55.22: Cast thy care, or thought, [[or thy busyness]], on the Lord, and he shall fully nourish thee; and he shall not give without end fluttering to a just [[or rightwise]] man.
55.23: But thou, God, shalt lead them forth; into the pit of death. Men-quellers and beguilers shall not have half their days; but, Lord, I shall hope in thee.

56.1: To the overcoming, on the dumb culver of far drawing away, the comely song of David, when the Philistines held him in Gath. God, have mercy on me, for a man hath defouled me; all day he impugned, and troubled me.
56.2: Mine enemies defouled me all day; for many fighters were against me.
56.3: Of the highness of day I shall dread; but God, I shall hope in thee.
56.4: In God I shall praise my words; I hoped in God, I shall not dread what thing flesh, or man, shall do to me.
56.5: All day they cursed my words; against me all their thoughts were into evil.
56.6: They shall dwell, and they shall hide; they shall ambush mine heel. As they abide my life,
56.7: for nought shalt thou make them safe; in ire thou shalt break altogether peoples.
56.8: God, I showed my life to thee; thou hast set [[or puttest]] my tears in thy sight. As and in thy promise, Lord;
56.9: then mine enemies shall be turned aback. In whatever day I shall inwardly call thee; lo! I have known, that thou art my God.
56.10: In God I shall praise a word; in the Lord I shall praise a word.
56.11: I shall hope in God; I shall not dread what thing man shall do to me.
56.12: God, thine avows [[or vows]] be in me; which I shall yield praisings to thee.
56.13: For thou hast delivered my life from death, and my feet from sliding; that I please before God in the light of them that live.

57.1: To the victory, lose thou not the seemly song, either the sweet song, of David, when he fled from the face of Saul into the den. God, have mercy on me, have thou mercy on me; for my soul trusteth in thee. And I shall hope in the shadow of thy wings; till wickedness pass.
57.2: I shall cry to God alder-highest; to God that did well to me.
57.3: He sent from heaven, and delivered me; he gave into shame them that defoul me. God sent his mercy and his truth,
57.4: and delivered my soul from the midst of whelps of lions; I slept troubled or disturbed. The sons of men, the teeth of them be armours [[or arms]] and arrows; and their tongue is a sharp sword.
57.5: God, be thou enhanced above heavens; and thy glory above all earth.
57.6: They made ready a snare to my feet; and they greatly bowed my life. They delved a ditch before my face; and they felled [[or fell]] down into it.
57.7: God, mine heart is ready, mine heart is ready; I shall sing, and I shall say psalm.
57.8: My glory, rise thou up; psaltery and harp, rise thou up; I shall rise up early.
57.9: Lord, I shall acknowledge to thee among peoples; and I shall say psalm [[to thee]] among heathen men.
57.10: For thy mercy is magnified till to heavens; and thy truth till to the clouds.
57.11: God, be thou enhanced above heavens; and thy glory above all earth.

58.1: To victory, lose thou not the sweet song, either the seemly psalm, of David. Forsooth if ye speak rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]] verily; ye sons of men, deem rightfully [[or evenly]].
58.2: For in heart ye work wickedness in earth; your hands make ready unrightfulnesses [[or unrightwisenesses]].
58.3: Sinners were made aliens from the womb; they erred from the womb, they spake false things.
58.4: Strong vengeance is to them, by the likeness of a serpent; as of a deaf snake, and stopping his ears.
58.5: Which shall not hear the voice of charmers; and of a venom-maker charming ever so wisely.
58.6: God shall all-break the teeth of them in their mouth; the Lord shall break altogether the great teeth of lions.
58.7: They shall come to nought, as water running away; he bent his bow, till they be made sick.
58.8: As wax that floateth [[or floweth]] away, they shall be taken away; fire fell above, and they saw not the sun.
58.9: Before that your thorns understood the rhamn, either thieve-thorn; he swalloweth them so in ire, as with living men.
58.10: The just [[or rightwise]] man shall be glad, when he shall see vengeance; he shall wash his hands in the blood of a sinner.
58.11: And a man shall say truly, For fruit is to a just [[or rightwise]] man; truly God is deeming them in earth.

59.1: To the overcomer, lose thou not the seemly song of David, when Saul sent men and kept the house, to slay him. My God, deliver thou me from mine enemies; and deliver thou me from them that rise against me.
59.2: Deliver thou me from them that work wickedness; and save thou me from men-quellers.
59.3: For lo! they have taken my soul; strong men fell in on me. Neither for my wickedness, neither for my sin;
59.4: Lord, I ran without wickedness, and dressed my works. Rise up into my meeting, and see;
59.5: and thou, Lord God of virtues, art God of Israel. Give thou attention to visit all folks; do thou not mercy to all that work wickedness.
59.6: They shall be turned at eventide, and they as dogs shall suffer hunger; and they shall compass, that is, go abegging in, the city.
59.7: Lo! they shall speak in their mouth, and a sword in their lips; for who heard?
59.8: And thou, Lord, shalt scorn them; thou shalt bring all folks to nought.
59.9: I shall keep my strength to thee; for God is mine up-taker,
59.10: my God, his mercy shall come before me. God showed to me my desire on mine enemies,
59.11: slay thou not them; lest any time my peoples forget. Scatter thou them in thy virtue; and, Lord, my defender, put thou them down.
59.12: Put down the trespass of their mouth, and the word of their lips; and be they taken in their pride. And of cursing and of leasing; they shall be showed in the ending.
59.13: In the ire of ending, and they shall not be; and they shall know, that the Lord shall be Lord of Jacob, and of the ends of earth.
59.14: They shall be turned at eventide, and they as dogs shall suffer hunger; and they shall compass, that is, go abegging in, the city.
59.15: They shall be scattered abroad, for to eat; soothly if they be not [[ful]] filled, and they shall grutch.
59.16: But I shall sing of thy strength; and early I shall enhance thy mercy. For thou art made mine up-taker; and my refuge, in the day of my tribulation.
59.17: Mine helper, I shall sing to thee; for thou art God, mine up-taker, my God, my mercy.

60.1: To victory, on the witnessing of the rose, the sweet song of David, to teach men, when he fought against Aram of floods, and Syria of Zobah; and Joab turned again, and smote Edom in the valley of salt pits, twelve thousand. God, thou hast put away us, and thou hast destroyed us; thou were wroth, and thou hast done mercy to us.
60.2: Thou movedest the earth, and thou troubledest it; make thou whole the sorrows thereof, for it is moved.
60.3: Thou showedest hard things to thy people; thou gavest drink to us with the wine of compunction.
60.4: Thou hast given a signifying to them that dread thee; that they flee from the face of the bow.
60.5: That thy darlings be delivered; make thou safe with thy right hand, and hear thou me.
60.6: God spake by [[or in]] his holy place; I shall be glad, and I shall part Shechem, and I shall mete [[or measure]] the great valley of tabernacles.
60.7: Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine; and Ephraim is the strength of mine head. Judah is my king;
60.8: Moab is the pot of mine hope. Into Idumea I shall stretch forth my shoe; aliens be made subject to me.
60.9: Who shall lead me into a city made strong; who shall lead me into Idumea?
60.10: Whether not thou, God, that hast put away us; and shalt thou not, God, go out in our virtues?
60.11: Lord, give thou to us help out of tribulation; for the help of man is vain.
60.12: In God we shall make virtue; and he shall bring to nought them that trouble or disturb us.

61.1: To victory, on organs, to David himself. God, hear thou my beseech-ing; give thou attention to my prayer.
61.2: From the ends of the land I cried to thee; the while mine heart was anguished, thou enhancedest me in a stone. Thou leddest me forth,
61.3: for thou art made mine hope; a tower of strength from the face of the enemy.
61.4: I shall dwell in thy tabernacle into worlds; I shall be covered in the covering of thy wings.
61.5: For thou, my God, hast heard my prayer; thou hast given heritage to them that dread thy name.
61.6: Thou shalt add, either increase, days on[[to]] the days of the king; his years till into the day of generation and of generation.
61.7: He dwelleth without end in the sight of God; who shall seek the mercy and truth of him?
61.8: So I shall say psalm to thy name into the world of world; that I yield my vows from day into day.

62.1: To victory, over Jeduthun, the psalm of David. Whether my soul shall not be subject to God; for mine health is of him.
62.2: For why he is both my God, and mine health; mine up-taker, I shall no more be moved.
62.3: How long fall ye on a man? all ye slain; as to a wall bowed, and as a wall of stone without mortar cast down.
62.4: Nevertheless they thought to put away my price, I ran in thirst; with their mouth they blessed, and in their heart they cursed.
62.5: Nevertheless, my soul, be thou subject to God; for my patience is of him.
62.6: For he is my God, and my saviour; mine helper, I shall not pass out.
62.7: Mine health, and my glory is in God; God is the giver of mine help, and mine hope is in God.
62.8: All the gathering together of the people, hope ye in God, pour ye out your hearts before him; God is our helper without end.
62.9: Nevertheless the sons of men be vain; the sons of men be liars in balances, that they deceive of vanity into the same thing.
62.10: Do not ye have hope in wicked-ness, and do not ye covet ravens; if riches be plenteous, do not ye set the heart thereto.
62.11: God spake once, I heard these two things; that power is of God,
62.12: and, thou Lord, mercy is to thee; for thou shalt yield to each man by his works.

63.1: The psalm of David, when he was in the desert of Judah. God, my God, I wake to thee full early. My soul thirsted to thee; my flesh thirsted to thee full manyfold. In a land forsaken without way, and without water,
63.2: so I appeared to thee in holy; that I should see thy virtue, and thy glory.
63.3: For thy mercy is better than lives or life itself; my lips shall praise thee.
63.4: So I shall bless thee in my life; and in thy name I shall raise mine hands.
63.5: My soul be [[ful]] filled as with inner fatness and uttermore fatness; and my mouth shall praise with lips of full out joying.
63.6: So I had mind on thee on my bed, in the morrowtides I shall think of thee;
63.7: for thou hast been mine helper. And in the covering of thy wings I shall make full out joy,
63.8: my soul cleaved after thee; thy right hand took me up.
63.9: Forsooth they sought in vain my life, they shall enter into the lower things of earth;
63.10: they shall be betaken into the hands of sword, they shall be made the parts of foxes.
63.11: But the king shall be glad in God; and all men shall be praised that swear in him; for the mouth of them, that speak wicked things, is stopped.

64.1: To victory, the psalm of David. God, hear thou my prayer, when I beseech; deliver thou my soul from dread of the enemy.
64.2: Thou hast defended me from the covent or convent of evil-doers; from the multitude of them that work wickedness.
64.3: For they sharpened their tongues as a sword, they bend their bow, a bitter thing;
64.4: for to shoot in huddles, or privates, him that is unwemmed. Suddenly they shall shoot him, and they shall not dread;
64.5: they made steadfast to themselves a wicked word. They told, that they should hide snares; they said, Who shall see them?
64.6: They sought wickednesses; they sought, and failed not in seeking. A man nighed to [[a]] deep heart;
64.7: and God shall be enhanced. The arrows of little men, that is, of envious men, be made the wounds of them;
64.8: and the tongues of them be made sick against them. All men be troubled, that saw them;
64.9: and each man dreaded. And they told the works of God; and they understood the deeds of him.
64.10: The just [[or rightwise]] man shall be glad in the Lord, and shall hope in him; and all men of rightful heart shall be praised.

65.1: To victory, the psalm of the song of David. God, praising becometh thee in Zion; and a vow shall be yielded to thee in Jerusalem.
65.2: Hear thou my prayer; each man shall come to thee.
65.3: The words of wicked men had the mastery over us; and thou shalt do mercy to our wickednesses.
65.4: Blessed is he, whom thou hast chosen, and hast taken; he shall dwell in thy foreyards. We shall be [[ful]] filled with the goods of thine house; thy temple is holy,
65.5: wonderful in equity. God, our health, hear thou us; thou art hope of all coasts of earth, and in the sea afar.
65.6: And thou makest ready hills in thy virtue, and art girded with power;
65.7: which troublest the depth of the sea, the sound of the waves thereof. Folks shall be troubled,
65.8: and they that dwell in the ends shall dread of thy signs; thou shalt delight the outgoings of the morrow-tide and eventide.
65.9: Thou hast visited the land, and hast greatly filled it; thou hast multiplied to make it rich. The flood of God was [[full-]]filled with waters; thou madest ready the meat of them, for the making ready thereof is so.
65.10: Thou filling greatly the streams thereof, multiply the fruits thereof; the land bringing forth fruits shall be glad in the gutters of it.
65.11: Thou shalt bless the crown of the year of thy good will; and thy fields shall be [[full-]]filled with plenty of fruits.
65.12: The fair things of desert shall wax fat; and little hills shall be encom-passed with full out joying.
65.13: The wethers of sheep be clothed, and valleys shall be plenteous of wheat; they shall cry out, and soothly they shall say praising or psalm.

66.1: To victory, the song of [[the]] psalm. All the earth, make ye joy heartily to God,
66.2: say ye psalm to his name; give ye glory to his praising.
66.3: Say ye to God, Lord, thy works be full dreadful; in the multitude of thy virtue thine enemies shall lie down to thee.
66.4: God, all the earth worship thee, and sing to thee; say it psalm to thy name.
66.5: Come ye and see ye the works of God; fearedful in counsels on the sons of men.
66.6: Which turned the sea into dry land; in the flood they shall pass [[through]] with foot, there we shall be glad in him.
66.7: The which is Lord in his virtue without end, his eyes behold on folks; they that make sharp be not enhanced in themselves.
66.8: Ye heathen men, bless our God; and make ye heard the voice of his praising.
66.9: That hath set my soul to life, and gave not my feet into stirring.
66.10: For thou, God, hast proved us; thou hast examined us by fire, as silver is examined.
66.11: Thou leddest us into a snare, thou puttedest tribulations in our back;
66.12: thou settedest [[or puttest]] men on our heads. We passed by [[or through]] fire and water; and thou leddest us out into refreshing.
66.13: I shall enter into thine house in burnt sacrifices; I shall yield to thee my vows,
66.14: which my lips spake distinctly. And my mouth spake in my tribulation;
66.15: I shall offer to thee burnt sacrifices full of marrow, with the burning of rams; I shall offer to thee oxes [[or oxen]] with bucks of goats.
66.16: All ye that dread God, come and hear, and I shall tell; how great things he hath done to my soul.
66.17: I cried to him with my mouth; and I joyed fully [[or full out joyed]] under my tongue.
66.18: If I beheld wickedness in mine heart; the Lord shall not hear.
66.19: Therefore God heard; and he per-ceived the voice of my beseeching.
66.20: Blessed be God; that removed not my prayer, nor his mercy from me.

67.1: To victory in organs, the psalm of the song. God have mercy on us, and bless us; lighten he his cheer on us, and have he mercy on us.
67.2: That we know thy way on earth; thine health in all folks.
67.3: God, peoples acknowledge to thee; all peoples acknowledge to thee.
67.4: Heathen men be glad, and make fully joy [[or and full out joy]], for thou deemest peoples in equity; and dressest heathen men in earth.
67.5: God, peoples acknowledge to thee, all peoples acknowledge to thee;
67.6: the earth hath given his fruit. God, our God, bless us,
67.7: God bless us; and all the coasts of earth dread him.

68.1: To victory, the psalm of the song of David. God rise up, and his enemies be scattered; and they that hate him, flee from his face.
68.2: As smoke faileth, fail they; as wax floateth [[or floweth]] from the face of fire, so perish [[the]] sinners from the face of God.
68.3: And just [[or rightwise]] men eat, and make they fully joy [[or full out glad they]] in the sight of God; and delight they in gladness.
68.4: Sing ye to God, say ye psalm to his name; make ye [[a]] way to him, that ascendeth [[or goeth up]] on the going down, the Lord is name of him. Make ye fully joy [[or Full out joyeth]] in his sight, his enemies shall be troubled from the face of him,
68.5: which is the father of fatherless and motherless children; and the judge of widows. God is in his holy place;
68.6: God that maketh men of one will to dwell in the house. Which leadeth out by strength them that be bound; in like manner them that make sharp [[or that stir]], that dwell in sepulchres.
68.7: God, when thou wentest out in the sight of thy people; when thou passedest forth in the desert.
68.8: The earth was moved, for heavens dropped down from the face of God of Sinai; from the face of God of Israel.
68.9: God, thou shalt impart willful rain to thine heritage, and it was sick; but thou madest it perfect.
68.10: Thy beasts shall dwell therein; God, thou hast made ready in thy sweetness to the poor man.
68.11: The Lord shall give a word; to them that preach the gospel with much virtue.
68.12: The kings of virtues be made loved of the darling; and to the fair-ness of the house to part spoils.
68.13: If ye sleep among the midst of sorts, either heritages, yet ye shall be as the feathers of the culver that be covered of silver; and the hinder things of the back thereof be in the shining of gold.
68.14: While the king of heaven deemeth kings thereon, they shall be made whiter than snow in Zalmon;
68.15: the hill of God is a fat hill. The crudded hill is a fat hill;
68.16: whereto believe ye falsely, ye crudded hills? The hill in which it pleaseth well God to dwell therein; for the Lord shall dwell into the end.
68.17: The chariot of God is manyfold with ten thousand, a thousand of them that be glad; the Lord was in them, in Sinai, in the holy place.
68.18: Thou ascendedest on high, thou tookest captivity captive; thou receiv-edest gifts among men. For why thou tookest also from them that believed not; for to dwell in the Lord God.
68.19: Blessed be the Lord each day; the God of our healths shall make an easy way to us.
68.20: Our God is God to make men safe; and outgoing [[or the going-out]] from death is of the Lord God.
68.21: Nevertheless God shall break the heads of his enemies; the top of the hair of them that go in their trespasses.
68.22: The Lord said, I shall turn from Bashan; I shall turn into the depth of the sea.
68.23: That thy foot be dipped in blood; the tongue of thy dogs be dipped in blood of the enemies of him.
68.24: God, they saw thy goings in; the goings-in [[or in-goings]] of my God, of my king, which is in the holy place.
68.25: Princes joined with singers came before; in the middle or in the midst of young damsels singing in tympans.
68.26: In churches bless ye God; bless ye the Lord from the wells of Israel.
68.27: There is Benjamin, a young man; in the ravishing of mind. The princes of Judah were the dukes of them; the princes of Zebulun, the princes of Naphtali.
68.28: God, command thou to thy virtue; God, confirm thou this thing, which thou hast wrought in us.
68.29: From thy temple, which is in Jerusalem; kings shall offer gifts to thee.
68.30: Blame thou the wild beasts of the reed, the gathering together of bulls is among the kine of peoples; that they exclude them that be proved by silver. Destroy thou folks that will or desire battles,
68.31: legates shall come from Egypt; Ethiopia shall come before the hands thereof to God.
68.32: Realms of the earth, sing ye to God; say ye psalm to the Lord. Sing ye to God;
68.33: that ascended [[or went up]] on the heaven of heaven at the east. Lo! he shall give to his voice the voice of virtue,
68.34: give ye glory to God on Israel; his great doing and his virtue is in the clouds.
68.35: God is wonderful in his saints; God of Israel, he shall give virtue, and strength, to his people; blessed be God.

69.1: To victory, on the roses of David. God, make thou me safe; for waters have entered unto my soul.
69.2: I am set in the slime of the depth; and there is no substance. I came into the depth of the sea; and the tempest drenched or drowned me [[down]].
69.3: I travailed crying, my cheeks were made hoarse; mine eyes failed, the while I hope/d into my God.
69.4: They that hated me without cause; were multiplied above the hairs of mine head. Mine enemies that pursued me unjustly were comforted; I paid then for those things, which I ravished not.
69.5: God, thou knowest mine unknow-ing; and my trespasses be not hid from thee.
69.6: Lord, Lord of virtues; they, that abide thee, be not ashamed in me. God of Israel; they, that seek thee, be not shamed on me.
69.7: For I suffered shame for thee; shame covered my face.
69.8: I am made a stranger to my brethren; and a pilgrim to the sons of my mother.
69.9: For the fervent love of thine house ate me; and the shames of men saying shames to thee fell on me.
69.10: And I covered my soul with fasting; and it was made into shame to me.
69.11: And I putted [[or put]] for my cloth an hair-shirt; and I am made to them into a parable.
69.12: They, that sat in the gate, spake against me; and they, that drank wine, sang of me.
69.13: But Lord, I dress my prayer to thee; God, I abide the time of good pleasance. Hear thou me in the multitude of thy mercy; in the truth of thine health.
69.14: Deliver thou me from the clay, that I be not fast set-in; deliver thou me from them that hate me, and from [[the]] depths or deepness of waters.
69.15: The tempest of water drench not me [[down]], neither the depth swallow me; neither the pit make strait his mouth on me.
69.16: Lord, hear thou me, for thy mercy is benign; after the multitude of thy merciful doings behold thou into me.
69.17: And turn not away thy face from thy servant; for I am in tribulation, hear thou me swiftly.
69.18: Give thou attention to my soul, and deliver thou it; for mine enemies, deliver thou me.
69.19: Thou knowest my reproof, and my despising; and my shame. All that trouble me be in thy sight;
69.20: mine heart abode in shame, and wretchedness. And I abode him, that was sorry together with me, and none was; and that should comfort me, and I found not.
69.21: And they gave gall into my meat; and in my thirst they gave to me drink with vinegar.
69.22: The board of them be made before them into a snare; and into yieldings, and into cause of stumbling.
69.23: Their eyes be made dark, that they see not; and ever[[more]] bow down the back of them.
69.24: Shed [[or Pour]] out thine ire [[or wrath]] on them; and the strong vengeance of thine ire take them.
69.25: The habitation of them be made forsaken; and be there none that dwell in the tabernacles of them.
69.26: For they pursued him, whom thou hast smitten; and they added on the sorrow of my wounds.
69.27: Add thou wickedness on the wickedness of them; and enter they not into thy rightwiseness.
69.28: Be they done away from the book of living men; and be they not written with just [[or rightwise]] men.
69.29: I am poor and sorrowful; God, thine health [[or salvation]] took me up.
69.30: I shall praise the name of God with song; and I shall magnify him with praising.
69.31: And it shall please God more than a new calf bringing forth horns and claws.
69.32: Poor men see, and be glad; seek ye God, and your soul shall live.
69.33: For the Lord heard poor men; and despised not his bound men.
69.34: Heavens and earth, praise him; the sea, and all creeping beasts in those, praise him.
69.35: For God shall make safe Zion; and the cities of Judah shall be builded. And they shall dwell there; and they shall get it by heritage.
69.36: And the seed of his servants shall have it in possession; and they that love his name, shall dwell therein.

70.1: To the victory, [[the psalm]] of David, to have mind. God, behold thou into mine help; Lord, haste thou to help me.
70.2: Be they shamed, and ashamed; that seek my life. Be they turned aback; and shame they, that will or desire evils to me.
70.3: Be they turned away anon, and shame they; that say to me, Well! well!
70.4: All men that seek thee, make fully joy [[or full out joy they]], and be glad in thee; and they that love thine health, say ever[[more]], The Lord be magnified.
70.5: Forsooth I am a needy man, and poor; God help thou me. Thou art mine helper and my deliverer; Lord, tarry thou not.

71.1: Lord, I hoped in thee; be I not shamed without end;
71.2: in thy rightwiseness deliver thou me, and ravish me out. Bow down thine ear to me; and make me safe.
71.3: Be thou to me into God a defender; and into a strengthened place, that thou make me safe. For thou art my steadfastness; and my refuge.
71.4: My God, deliver thou me from the hand of the sinner; and from the hand of a man doing against the law, and of the wicked man.
71.5: For thou, Lord, art my patience; Lord, thou art mine hope from my youth.
71.6: In thee I am confirmed, that is, defended, from the womb; thou art my defender from the womb of my mother. My singing is ever[[more]] in thee;
71.7: I am made as a great wonder to many men; and thou art a strong helper.
71.8: My mouth be filled with praising; that I sing thy glory, all day thy great-ness.
71.9: Cast thou not away me in the time of eld age /in the time of oldness; when my strength faileth, forsake thou not me.
71.10: For mine enemies said of me; and they that kept my life made counsel together.
71.11: Saying, God hath forsaken him; pursue ye, and take him; for none there is that shall deliver.
71.12: God, be thou not made afar from me; my God, behold thou into mine help.
71.13: Men that backbite my soul, be shamed, and fail they; and be they covered with reproof and shame, that seek evils to me.
71.14: But I shall hope ever[[more]]; and I shall add to ever over all thy praising.
71.15: My mouth shall tell thy rightful-ness [[or rightwiseness]]; all day thine health. For I knew not by literature, that is, by man’s teaching, but by God’s revelation,
71.16: I shall enter into the powers of the Lord; Lord, I shall bethink on thy rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]] alone.
71.17: God, thou hast taught me from my youth, and till to now; I shall tell out thy marvels.
71.18: And till into eld age /into oldness, and the last age; God, forsake thou not me. Till I tell thine arm, or power, to each generation that shall come.
71.19: Till I tell of thy might, and thy rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]], God, till into the highest great deeds which thou hast done; God, who is like thee?
71.20: How great tribulations, many and evil, hast thou showed to me; and thou converted, hast quickened me, and hast again-brought me again from the depths of earth.
71.21: Thou hast multiplied thy great doing; and thou converted, hast comforted me.
71.22: For why and I shall acknowledge to thee, thou God, thy truth in the instruments of psalm; I shall sing in an harp to thee, that art the holy of Israel.
71.23: My lips shall make fully joy [[or full out joy]], when I shall sing to thee; and my soul, which thou again-boughtest.
71.24: But and my tongue shall think all day on thy rightfulness [[or rightwise-ness]]; when they shall be shamed and ashamed, that seek evils to me.

72.1: To Solomon. God, give thy doom to the king; and thy rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]] to the son of the king.
72.2: To deem thy people in rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]]; and thy poor men in doom.
72.3: Mountains receive peace to the people; and little hills receive rightful-ness [[or rightwiseness]].
72.4: He shall deem the poor men of the people, and he shall make safe the sons of poor men; and he shall make low the false challenger.
72.5: And he shall dwell with the sun, and before the moon, that is, without beginning, and end; in generation and into generation.
72.6: He shall come down as rain into a fleece; and as gutters dropping on the earth.
72.7: Rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]] shall come forth in his days; and the abun-dance of peace, till the moon be taken away.
72.8: And he shall be lord from the sea till to the sea; and from the flood till to the ends of the world.
72.9: Ethiopians shall fall down before him; and his enemies shall lick the earth.
72.10: The kings of Tarshish and isles shall offer gifts; the kings of Arabia and of Seba shall bring gifts.
72.11: And all kings shall worship him; all folks shall serve him.
72.12: For he shall deliver a poor man from the mighty; and a poor man to whom there was none helper.
72.13: He shall spare a poor man and needy; and he shall make safe the souls of poor men.
72.14: He shall again-buy the souls of them from usuries, and wickedness; and the name of them is honourable before him.
72.15: And he shall live, and men shall give to him of the gold of Arabia; and they shall ever worship of him, all day they shall bless him.
72.16: Steadfastness shall be in the earth, in the highest place of mountains; the fruit thereof shall be enhanced above the Lebanon; and they shall blossom from the city, as the hay of earth doeth.
72.17: His name be blessed into worlds; his name dwell before the sun. And all the lineages of earth shall be blessed in him; all folks shall magnify him.
72.18: Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; which alone maketh marvels.
72.19: And blessed be the name of his majesty without end; and all earth shall be filled with his majesty; be it done, be it done.
72.20: The prayers, [[or praisings, or hymns]], of David, the son of Jesse, be ended.

73.1: The psalm of Asaph. God of Israel is full good; to them that be of rightful [[or right]] heart.
73.2: But my feet were moved almost; my steps were shed [[or poured]] out almost.
73.3: For I loved fervently on wicked men; seeing the peace of sinners.
73.4: For beholding is not to the death of them; and steadfastness in the sick-ness of them.
73.5: They be not in travail of other men; and they shall not be beaten with men.
73.6: Therefore pride hath held them; they were covered with their wicked-ness and unfaithfulness.
73.7: The wickedness of them came forth as of fatness; they went into desire of heart.
73.8: They thought and spake wayward-ness; they spake wickedness on high.
73.9: They putted [[or put]] their mouth into heaven; and their tongue passed in [[the]] earth.
73.10: Therefore my people shall be turned again here; and full days shall be found in them.
73.11: And they said, How knoweth God; and whether knowing is on high?
73.12: Lo! those sinners and having abundance in the world; held riches.
73.13: And I said, Therefore without cause I justified mine heart; and washed mine hands among innocents.
73.14: And I was beaten all day; and my chastising was in morrowtides.
73.15: If I said, I shall tell thus; lo! I [[have]] reproved the nation of thy sons.
73.16: I guessed, that I should know this; but too much travail is before me.
73.17: Till I enter into the saintuary of God; and understand in the last things of them.
73.18: Nevertheless for guiles [[or treach-eries]] thou hast put to them; thou castedest them down, while they were raised.
73.19: How be they made into desolation; they failed suddenly, they perished for their wickedness or waywardness.
73.20: As the dream of men that rise; Lord, thou shalt drive their image to nought, in thy city.
73.21: For mine heart is enflamed, and my reins be changed;
73.22: and I am driven to nought, and I knew not. As a work beast I am made with thee;
73.23: and I am ever with thee. Thou heldest my right hand,
73.24: and in thy will thou leddest me forth; and with glory thou tookest me up.
73.25: For why what is to me in heaven; and what would or desire I of thee on earth?
73.26: My flesh and mine heart failed; God of mine heart, and my part is God without end.
73.27: For lo! they that draw away far themselves from thee shall perish; thou hast lost all men that do forni-cation from thee.
73.28: But it is good to me to cleave to God; and to set [[or put]] mine hope in the Lord God. That I tell all thy preachings, in the gates of the daughter of Zion.

74.1: The learning of Asaph. God, why hast thou put us away into the end; thy strong vengeance is wroth on the sheep of thy pasture?
74.2: Be thou mindful of thy gathering together; which thou haddest in possession from the beginning. Thou again-boughtest the rod of thine heritage; the hill of Zion, in which thou dwelledest therein.
74.3: Raise thine hands into the prides of them; how great things the enemy did wickedly in the holy place.
74.4: And they that hated thee; had glory in the midst of thy solemnity. They setted their signs, either banners, to be signs on the highest place, as in the outgoing [[or going out]]; and they knew not.
74.5: As in a wood of trees, they hewed down with axes the gates thereof into itself;
74.6: they casted down it with an ax, and a broad falling ax.
74.7: They burnt with fire thy saintuary; they defouled the tabernacle of thy name in earth.
74.8: The kindred of them said together in their heart; Make we all the feast days of God to cease in the earth.
74.9: We have not seen our signs, now there is no prophet; and he shall no more know us.
74.10: God, how long shall the enemy say despite? the adversary stirreth to ire thy name into the end.
74.11: Why turnest thou away thine hand, to not draw out thy right hand from the midst of thy bosom, till into the end?
74.12: Forsooth God our king before worlds, wrought health in the midst of [[the]] earth.
74.13: Thou madest firm the sea by thy virtue; thou hast troubled the heads of the dragons in waters.
74.14: Thou hast broken the heads of the dragon; thou hast given him to be meat to the peoples of Ethiopians.
74.15: Thou hast broken wells, and strands [[or streams]]; thou madest dry the floods of Eitan.
74.16: The day is thine, and the night is thine; thou madest the morrowtide and the sun.
74.17: Thou madest all the ends of the earth; summer, and ver time, either springing time, thou formedest those [[or them]].
74.18: Be thou mindful of this thing, the enemy hath said shame to the Lord; and the unwise people hath excited to ire thy name.
74.19: Betake thou not to beasts men acknowledging to thee; and forget thou not into the end the souls of thy poor men.
74.20: Behold into thy testament; for they that be made dark of earth, be [[full-]]filled with the houses of wickednesses.
74.21: A meek man be not turned away made ashamed; a poor man and needy shall praise thy name.
74.22: God, rise up, deem thou thy cause; be thou mindful of thy shames, either upbraidings, of those that be all day of the unwise man.
74.23: Forget thou not the voices of thine enemies; the pride of them that hate thee ascendeth [[or goeth up]] ever-[[more]].

75.1: To the overcomer, lose thou not the psalm of the song of Asaph. God, we shall acknowledge to thee, we shall acknowledge; and we shall inwardly call thy name. We shall tell thy marvels;
75.2: when I shall take hold of the time, I shall deem with rightfulnesses.
75.3: The earth is melted, and all that dwell therein; I confirmed the pillars thereof.
75.4: I said to wicked men, Do not ye do wickedly; and to trespassers, Do not ye enhance the horn.
75.5: Do not ye raise on high your horn; do not ye speak wickedness against God.
75.6: For promotion cometh neither from the east, neither from the west, neither from desert hills;
75.7: for God is the judge. He meeketh this man, and enhanceth him;
75.8: for a cup of clean wine, full of meddling [[or mingling]], is in the hand of the Lord. And he bowed of this into that; nevertheless the dregs thereof is not diminished, either made less, for all [[the]] sinners of [[the]] earth shall drink thereof.
75.9: Forsooth I shall tell into the world; I shall sing to God of Jacob.
75.10: And I shall break all the horns of sinners; and the horns of the just [[or rightwise]] man shall be enhanced.

76.1: To the victory in organs, the psalm of the song of Asaph. God is known in Judah; his name is great in Israel.
76.2: And his place is made in peace; and his dwelling is in Zion.
76.3: There he brake powers; bow, shield, sword, and battle.
76.4: And thou, God, lightenest wonder-fully coming back from everlasting hills;
76.5: all unwise men of heart were troubled. They slept their sleep, that is, were dead; and all men found nothing of riches in their hands.
76.6: They that ascended [[or went up]] on horses; slept for thy blaming, thou God of Jacob.
76.7: Thou art fearful, and who shall against-stand thee? from that time of thine ire.
76.8: From heaven thou madest doom heard; the earth trembled, and rested.
76.9: When God rose up into doom; to make safe all the mild men of earth.
76.10: For the thought of man shall acknowledge to thee; and the remnants or leavings of thought shall make a feast day to thee.
76.11: Make ye a vow, and yield ye to your Lord God; all that bring gifts in the compass of it. To God fearedful,
76.12: and to him that taketh away the spirit of princes; to the fearedful at the kings of earth.

77.1: To the victory on Jeduthun, the psalm of Asaph. With my voice I cried to the Lord, with my voice to God; and he gave attention to me.
77.2: In the day of my tribulation I sought God with mine hands; in the night before or toward him, and I am not deceived. My soul forsook to be comforted;
77.3: I was mindful of God, and I delighted, and I was exercised; and my spirit failed.
77.4: Mine eyes before took wakings; I was troubled, and I spake not.
77.5: I thought on eld [[or old]] days; and I had in mind everlasting years.
77.6: And I thought in the night with mine heart; and I was exercised, and I cleansed my spirit.
77.7: Whether God shall cast away with-out end; either shall he not lay to, that he be more pleased yet?
77.8: Either shall he cut away his mercy into the end; from generation into generation?
77.9: Either shall God forget to do mercy; either shall he withhold his mercies in his ire [[or wrath]]?
77.10: And I said, Now I began; this is the changing of the right hand of the high God.
77.11: I had mind on the works of the Lord; for I shall have mind from the beginning of thy marvels.
77.12: And I shall think on all thy works; and I shall be exercised, either occupied, in thy findings.
77.13: God, thy way was in the holy place; what God is great as our God?
77.14: thou art God, that doest marvels. Thou madest thy virtue known among peoples;
77.15: thou again-boughtest in thine arm thy people, the sons of Jacob and of Joseph.
77.16: God, waters saw thee, waters saw thee, and dreaded; and depths of waters were troubled.
77.17: The multitude of the sound of waters; clouds gave voice. For why thine arrows pass [[through]];
77.18: the voice of thy thunder was in a wheel. Thy lightnings shined to the world; the earth was moved, and trembled.
77.19: Thy way in the sea, and thy paths in many waters; and thy steps shall not be known.
77.20: Thou leddest forth thy people as sheep; in the hand of Moses and Aaron.

78.1: The learning of Asaph. My people, perceive ye my law; bow your ear into the words of my mouth.
78.2: I shall open my mouth in parables; I shall speak perfect reasons [[or propositions]] from the beginning.
78.3: How great things have we heard, and we have known those [[or them]]; and our fathers told to us.
78.4: Those [[or They]] be not hid from the sons of them; in another generation. And they told the praisings of the Lord, and the virtues of him; and his marvels, which he did.
78.5: And he raised witnessing in Jacob; and he setted law in Israel. How great things commanded he to our fathers, to make those known to their sons;
78.6: that another generation know. Sons, that shall be born, and shall rise up; shall tell out to their sons.
78.7: That they set [[or put]] their hope in God, and forget not the works of God; and that they seek or search his commandments.
78.8: Lest they be made a shrewd generation; and stirring to wrath, as the fathers of them. A generation that dressed not his heart; and his spirit was not believed with God.
78.9: The sons of Ephraim, bending a bow, and sending arrows; were turned in the day of battle.
78.10: They kept not the testament of God; and they would not go in his law.
78.11: And they forgat his benificences [[or benefits]]; and his marvels, which he showed to them.
78.12: He did marvels before the fathers of them, in the land of Egypt; in the field of Tanis.
78.13: He brake the sea, and led them through it; and he ordained the waters as in a bouget [[or bottle]].
78.14: And he led them forth in a cloud of the day; and all night in the lightening of fire.
78.15: He brake a stone in desert; and he gave water to them as in a much depth.
78.16: And he led water out of the stone; and he led forth waters as floods.
78.17: And they putted yet to do sin against him; they excited the high God into ire, in a place without water.
78.18: And they tempted God in their hearts; that they asked meats to their lives.
78.19: And they spake evil of God; they said, Whether God may make ready a board in desert?
78.20: For he smote a stone, and waters flowed; and streams went out in abundance. Whether also he may give bread; either make ready a board to his people?
78.21: Therefore the Lord heard, and delayed; and fire was kindled in Jacob, and the ire of God ascended [[or went up]] on Israel.
78.22: For they believed not in God; neither hoped in his health.
78.23: And he commanded to the clouds above; and he opened the gates of heaven.
78.24: And he rained to them manna for to eat; and he gave to them bread of heaven.
78.25: Man ate the bread of angels; he sent to them meats in abundance.
78.26: He turned over the south wind from heaven; and he brought in by his virtue the west wind.
78.27: And he rained fleshes as dust on them; and also volatiles feathered, as the gravel of the sea.
78.28: And those felled in the midst of their castles [[or they fell in the middle of the tents of them]]; about the taber-nacles of them.
78.29: And they ate, and were filled greatly, and he brought their desire to them;
78.30: they were not defrauded of their desire. Yet their meats were in their mouth;
78.31: and the wrath of God ascended [[or went up]] on them. And he killed the fat men of them; and he hindered the chosen men of Israel.
78.32: In all these things they sinned yet; and believed not in the marvels of God.
78.33: And the days of them failed in vanity; and the years of them failed with haste.
78.34: When he killed them, they sought him; and they turned again, and early they came to him.
78.35: And they bethought, that God is the helper of them; and the high God is the again-buyer of them.
78.36: And they loved him in their mouth; and with their tongue they lied to him.
78.37: Forsooth the heart of them was not rightful [[or right]] with him; neither they were had faithful in his testament.
78.38: But he is merciful, and he shall be made merciful to the sins of them; and he shall not destroy them. And he did greatly, to turn away his ire; and he kindled not all his ire.
78.39: And he bethought, that they be flesh; a spirit going, and not turning again.
78.40: How oft made they him wroth in desert; they stirred him into ire in a place without water.
78.41: And they were turned, and tempted God; and they wrathed the Holy of Israel.
78.42: They bethought not on his hand; in the day in which he again-bought them from the hand of the troubler.
78.43: As he setted [[or put]] his signs in Egypt; and his great wonders in the field of Tanis.
78.44: And he turned the floods of them, and the rains of them, into blood; that they should not drink.
78.45: He sent a flesh fly [[or hound flea]] into them, and it ate them; and he sent a paddock [[or frog]], and it lost them.
78.46: And he gave the fruits of them to rust; and he gave the travails of them to locusts.
78.47: And he killed the vines of them with hail; and the sycamore trees of them with frost.
78.48: And he betook the beasts of them to hail; and the possessions of them to fire.
78.49: He sent into them the ire of his indignation; indignation, and ire, and tribulation, sendings-in by evil angels.
78.50: He made a way to the path of his ire, and he spared not from the death of their lives; and he enclosed alto-gether in death the beasts of them.
78.51: And he smote all the first engen-dered things [[or first begotten]] in the land of Egypt; the first fruits of all the travail of them in the tabernacles of Ham.
78.52: And he took away his people as sheep; and he led them forth as a flock in desert.
78.53: And he led them forth in hope, and they dreaded not; and the sea covered the enemies of them.
78.54: And he brought them into the hill of his hallowing; into the hill which his right hand gat.
78.55: And he casted out heathen men from the face of them; and by lot he parted to them the land in a cord of dealing. And he made the lineages of Israel to dwell in the tabernacles of them.
78.56: And they tempted, and wrathed the high God; and they kept not his witnessings.
78.57: And they turned away themselves, and they kept not covenant; as their fathers they were turned into a shrewd bow.
78.58: They stirred him into ire in their little hills; and they stirred him to indignation in their graven images.
78.59: God heard, and forsook; and brought to nought Israel greatly.
78.60: And he putted [[or put]] away the tabernacle of Shiloh; his tabernacle in which he dwelled among men.
78.61: And he betook the virtue of them into captivity; and the fairness of them into the hands of the enemy.
78.62: And he enclosed altogether his people in sword; and he despised his heritage.
78.63: Fire ate the young men of them; and the virgins of them were not bewailed or bewept.
78.64: The priests of them fell down by sword; and the widows of them were not bewept.
78.65: And the Lord was raised, as sleeping; as mighty greatly filled [[or drunk]] of wine.
78.66: And he smote his enemies on the hinder parts; he gave to them ever-lasting shame.
78.67: And he putted [[or put]] away the tabernacle of Joseph; and he chose not the lineage of Ephraim.
78.68: But he chose the lineage of Judah; he chose the hill of Zion, which he loved.
78.69: And he as an unicorn builded his holy place; in the land, which he founded into worlds.
78.70: And he chose David his servant, and took him up from the flocks of sheep;
78.71: he took him from behind sheep with lambs. To feed Jacob his servant; and Israel his heritage.
78.72: And he fed them in the inno-cence of his heart; and he led them forth in the understandings of his hands.

79.1: The psalm of Asaph. God, heathen men came into thine heritage; they defouled thine holy temple, they setted [[or put]] Jerusalem into the keeping of apples.
79.2: They setted [[or put]] the slain bodies of thy servants to be meats to the volatiles of heavens; the fleshes of thy saints to the beasts of the earth.
79.3: They shedded out the blood of them, as water in the compass of Jerusalem; and none there was that buried them.
79.4: We be made a shame to our neighbours; mocking and scorning to them, that be in our compass.
79.5: Lord, how long shalt thou be wroth into the end? shall thy vengeance be kindled as fire?
79.6: Pour out thine ire into heathen men, that know not thee; and into realms, that called not thy name.
79.7: For they ate Jacob; and made desolate his place.
79.8: Have thou not mind on our eld [[or old]] wickednesses; thy mercies before take us soon, for we be made poor greatly.
79.9: God, our health, help thou us, and, Lord, for the glory of thy name, deliver thou us; and be thou merciful to our sins, for thy name.
79.10: Lest peradventure they say among heathen men, Where is the God of them? and be he known among nations before our eyes. The vengeance of the blood of thy servants, which is shed [[or poured]] out;
79.11: the wailing of fettered men enter into thy sight. After the greatness of thine arm; wield thou the sons of slain men.
79.12: And yield thou to our neighbours sevenfold in the bosom of them; the shame of them, which they did shame-fully to thee, thou Lord.
79.13: But we that be thy people, and the sheep of thy pasture; shall acknowledge to thee into the world. In generation and into generation, we shall tell thy praising.

80.1: To victory; this psalm is the wit-nessing of Asaph for lilies. Thou that governest Israel, give attention; that leadest forth Joseph as a sheep. Thou that sittest on cherubim, be showed
80.2: before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh. Stir thy power, and come thou, that thou make us safe.
80.3: God of virtues, turn [[or convert]] thou us; and show thy face, and we shall be safe.
80.4: Lord God of virtues, how long shalt thou be wroth on the prayer of thy servants?
80.5: How long shalt thou feed us with the bread of tears; and shalt give drink to us with tears in great measure?
80.6: Thou hast set [[or put]] us into against-saying to our neighbours; and our enemies have scorned us.
80.7: God of virtues, turn [[or convert]] thou us; and show thy face, and we shall be safe.
80.8: Thou translatedest or brought over a vine from Egypt; thou castedest out heathen men, and plantedest it.
80.9: Thou were leader of the way in the sight thereof; and thou plantedest the roots thereof, and it filled the land.
80.10: The shadow thereof covered hills; and the branches thereof filled the cedars of God.
80.11: It stretched forth his scions till to the sea, and the generations thereof till to the flood.
80.12: Why hast thou destroyed the wall thereof; and all men that go forth by the way, gather away the grapes thereof?
80.13: A boar of the wood destroyed it; and a singular wild beast devoured it.
80.14: God of virtues, be thou turned again to us; behold from heaven, and see, and visit this vine.
80.15: And make thou it perfect, which thy right hand planted; and behold thou on the son of man, which thou hast confirmed to thee.
80.16: Things were burnt with fire, and undermined; they who did this shall perish for the blaming of thy cheer.
80.17: Thine hand be made on the man of thy right hand; and on the son of man, whom thou hast confirmed to thee.
80.18: And we departed not from thee; thou shalt quicken us, and we shall inwardly call thy name.
80.19: Lord God of virtues, turn thou us; and show thy face, and we shall be safe.

81.1: To the overcomer, on the pressers [[or wine presses]], [[the psalm]] of Asaph. Make ye fully joy [[or Full out joyeth]] to God, our helper; sing ye heartily to God of Jacob.
81.2: Take ye a psalm, and give ye a tympan; a merry psaltery with an harp.
81.3: Blow ye with a trump in the new moon; in the noble day of your solemnity.
81.4: For why commandment is in Israel; and doom is to God of Jacob.
81.5: He setted [[or put]] that witnessing in Joseph; when he went out of the land of Egypt, he heard a language, that he knew not.
81.6: He turned away his back from burdens; his hands served in a coffin.
81.7: In tribulation thou inwardly called-est me, and I delivered thee; I heard thee in the hid place of tempest, I proved thee at the waters of against-saying.
81.8: My people, hear thou me, and I shall be witness against thee; Israel, if thou hearest me,
81.9: a fresh God shall not be in thee; and thou shalt not worship an alien god.
81.10: For I am thy Lord God, that led thee out of the land of Egypt; make large thy mouth, and I shall fill it.
81.11: And my people heard not my voice; and Israel gave not attention to me.
81.12: And I let them go after the desires of their heart; they shall go in their findings.
81.13: If my people had heard me; if Israel had gone in my ways.
81.14: For not in hap I had made low their enemies; and I had sent mine hand on men doing tribulation to them.
81.15: The enemies of the Lord lied or lay down to him; and their time shall be into worlds.
81.16: And he fed them with the fatness of wheat; and he [[ful]] filled them with honey of the stone.

82.1: The psalm of Asaph. God stood in the synagogue of gods; forsooth he deemeth gods in the middle.
82.2: How long deem ye with wicked-ness; and take the faces of sinners?
82.3: Deem ye to the needy man, and to the motherless child; justify ye the meek man and poor.
82.4: Ravish ye out a poor man; and deliver ye a needy man from the hand of the sinner.
82.5: They know not, neither under-stand, they go in darknesses; all the foundaments of [[the]] earth shall be moved.
82.6: I said, Ye be gods; and all ye be the sons of the high God.
82.7: But ye shall die as men; and ye shall fall down as one of the princes.
82.8: Rise, thou God, deem thou the earth; for thou shalt have heritage in all folks.

83.1: The song of the psalm of Asaph. God, who shall be like thee? God, be thou not still, neither be thou peaced.
83.2: For lo! thine enemies sounded; and they that hate thee raised the head.
83.3: They made a wicked counsel on thy people; and they thought against thy saints.
83.4: They said, Come ye, and lose we them from the folk; and the name of Israel be no more had in mind.
83.5: For they thought with one accord;
83.6: the tabernacles of Idumeans, and men of Ishmael disposed a testament together against thee. Moab, and Hag-arenes,
83.7: Gebal, and Ammon, and Amalek; and the aliens with them that dwell in Tyre.
83.8: For Assur cometh with them; they be made into help to the sons of Lot.
83.9: Make thou to them as to Midian, and Sisera; as to Jabin, in the strand [[or stream]] of Kishon.
83.10: They perished in Endor; they were made as a turd of earth.
83.11: Put thou the princes of them as Oreb and Zeeb; and Zebah and Zalmunna.
83.12: All the princes of them, that said, Hold we by heritage the saintuary of God.
83.13: My God, put thou them as a wheel; and as stubble before the face of the wind.
83.14: As fire that burneth a wood; and as flame burning hills.
83.15: So thou shalt pursue them in thy tempest; and thou shalt trouble them in thine ire.
83.16: Lord, fill thou the faces of them with shame; and they shall seek thy name.
83.17: Be they ashamed, and be they troubled into the world of world; and be they shamed, and perish they.
83.18: And know they, that Lord is name to thee; thou alone art the Highest in every land.

84.1: To victory, on the pressers [[or wine presses]]. The psalm of the sons of Korah. Lord of virtues, thy taber-nacles be greatly loved;
84.2: my soul coveteth, and faileth into the porches of the Lord. Mine heart, and my flesh; full out joyed into quick God [[or God alive]].
84.3: For why a sparrow findeth an house to itself; and a turtle findeth a nest to itself, where it shall keep his birds. Lord of virtues, thine altars; my king, and my God.
84.4: Lord, blessed be they that dwell in thine house; they shall praise thee into the worlds of worlds.
84.5: Blessed is the man, whose help is of thee; he hath ordained thy goings in his heart,
84.6: in the valley of tears, in the place which he hath set. For the giver of the law shall give blessing,
84.7: they shall go from virtue into virtue to strength; God of gods shall be seen in Zion.
84.8: Lord God of virtues, hear thou my prayer; God of Jacob, perceive thou with ears.
84.9: God, our defender, behold thou; and behold into the face of thy christ or thine anointed.
84.10: For why one day in thine halls is better; than a thousand elsewhere. I choose to be abject, either an outcast, in the house of my God; more than to dwell in the tabernacles of sinners.
84.11: For God loveth mercy and truth; the Lord shall give grace and glory. He shall not deprive them from goods, that go in innocence;
84.12: Lord of virtues, blessed is the man, that hopeth in thee.

85.1: To the overcomer, the song of the sons of Korah. Lord, thou hast blessed thy land; thou hast turned away the captivity of Jacob.
85.2: Thou hast forgiven the wicked-ness of thy people; thou hast covered all the sins of them.
85.3: Thou hast assuaged all thine ire; thou hast turned away from the ire of thine indignation.
85.4: God, our health, convert thou us; and turn away thine ire from us.
85.5: Whether thou shalt be wroth to us without end; either shalt thou hold forth thine ire from generation into generation?
85.6: God, thou converted, shalt quicken us; and thy people shall be glad in thee.
85.7: Lord, show thy mercy to us; and give thine health to us.
85.8: I shall hear what the Lord God shall speak in me; for he shall speak peace to his people. And on his holy men; and on them that be turned to heart.
85.9: Nevertheless his health is nigh men dreading him; that glory dwell in our land.
85.10: Mercy and truth met themselves; rightwiseness and peace were kissed.
85.11: Truth came forth of the earth; and rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]] beheld from heaven.
85.12: For the Lord shall give benignity; and our earth shall give his fruit.
85.13: Rightfulness [[or Rightwiseness]] shall go before him; and shall set his steps in the way.

86.1: The prayer of David. Lord, bow down thine ear, and hear me; for I am needy and poor.
86.2: Keep thou my life, for I am holy; my God, make thou safe thy servant hoping in thee.
86.3: Lord, have thou mercy on me, for I cried all day to thee;
86.4: make thou glad the soul of thy servant; for why, Lord, I have raised my soul to thee.
86.5: For thou, Lord, art sweet and mild; and of much mercy to all men inwardly calling thee.
86.6: Lord, perceive thou my prayer with ears; and give thou attention to the voice of my beseeching.
86.7: In the day of my tribulation I cried to thee; for thou heardest me.
86.8: Lord, none among gods is like thee; and none is even to thy works.
86.9: Lord, all folks, whichever thou madest, shall come, and worship before thee; and they shall glorify thy name.
86.10: For thou art full great, and making marvels; thou art God alone.
86.11: Lord, lead thou me forth in thy way, and I shall enter in thy truth; mine heart be glad, that it dread thy name.
86.12: My Lord God, I shall acknowledge to thee in all mine heart; and I shall glorify thy name without end.
86.13: For thy mercy is great on me; and thou deliveredest my soul from the lower hell.
86.14: God, wicked men have risen upon me; and the synagogue of mighty men have sought my life; and they have not set forth thee in their sight.
86.15: And thou, Lord God, doing mercy, and merciful; patient, and of much mercy, and soothfast.
86.16: Behold on me, and have mercy on me, give thou the empire to thy servant; and make thou safe the son of thine handmaid.
86.17: Make thou with me a sign in good, that they see, that hate me, and be ashamed; for thou, Lord, hast helped or holpen me, and hast comforted me.

87.1: The psalm of the song of the sons of Korah. The foundaments thereof be in holy hills;
87.2: the Lord loveth the gates of Zion, more than all the tabernacles of Jacob.
87.3: Thou city of God, without end; glorious things be said of thee.
87.4: I shall be mindful of Rahab, and Babylon; knowing me. Lo! aliens, and Tyre, and the people of Ethiopians; they were there.
87.5: Whether a man shall say to Zion, And a man is born therein; and that man, alder Highest, founded it?
87.6: The Lord shall tell in the scriptures of these peoples; and of these princes, that were therein.
87.7: As the dwelling of all that be glad; is in thee.

88.1: The song of the psalm, to the sons of Korah, to victory on Mahalath, for to answer the learning of Heman the Ezrahite. Lord God of mine health; I cried in day and night before thee.
88.2: My prayer enter before thy sight; bow down thine ear to my prayer.
88.3: For my soul is [[full-]]filled with evils; and my life nighed to hell.
88.4: I am guessed with them that go down into the pit; I am made as a man without help,
88.5: and free among dead men. As men wounded sleeping in sepulchres, of which men none thou is mindful of after; and they be put away from thine hand.
88.6: They have put me in the lower pit; in dark places, and in the shadow of death.
88.7: Thy strong vengeance is confirmed on me; and thou hast brought in all thy waves on me.
88.8: Thou hast made far from me my known; they have set [[or put]] me abom-ination to themselves. I am taken in, and I went not out;
88.9: mine eyes were sick [[or enfeebled]] for poverty. Lord, I cried to thee; all day I spreaded abroad mine hands to thee.
88.10: Whether thou shalt do marvels to dead men; either leeches shall raise them up, and they shall acknowledge to thee?
88.11: Whether any man in sepulchre shall tell thy mercy; and thy truth in perdition?
88.12: Whether thy marvels shall be known in darknesses; and thy right-fulness [[or rightwiseness]] in the land of forgetting?
88.13: And, Lord, I cried to thee; and early my prayer shall before come to thee.
88.14: Lord, why puttest thou away my prayer; thou turnest away thy face from me?
88.15: I am poor, and in travails from my youth; soothly I am enhanced, and I am made low, and troubled.
88.16: Thy wraths passed on me; and thy dreads troubled me.
88.17: They encompassed me as water all day; they encompassed me altogether.
88.18: Thou madest far from me a friend and neighbour; and my known from wretchedness.

89.1: The learning of Ethan the Ezrahite. I shall sing without end; the mercies of the Lord. In generation and into generation; I shall tell thy truth with my mouth.
89.2: For thou saidest, Without end mercy shall be builded in heavens; thy truth shall be made ready in those [[or them]].
89.3: Thou saidest, I disposed a testa-ment to my chosen men; I swore to David, my servant,
89.4: till into without end I shall make ready thy seed. And I shall build thy seat; in generation, and into generation.
89.5: Lord, heavens shall acknowledge thy marvels; and thy truth in the church of saints.
89.6: For who in the clouds shall be made even to the Lord; shall be like God among the sons of God?
89.7: God, that is glorified in the council of saints; is great, and dreadful over all that be in his compass.
89.8: Lord God of virtues, who is like thee? Lord, thou art mighty, and thy truth is in thy compass.
89.9: Thou art Lord of the power of the sea; forsooth thou assuagest the stirring of the waves thereof.
89.10: Thou madest low the proud, as wounded; in the arm of thy strength thou hast scattered thine enemies.
89.11: Heavens be thine, and the earth is thine; thou hast founded the world, and the fullness thereof;
89.12: thou madest of nought the north and the sea. Tabor and Hermon shall make full out joy in thy name;
89.13: thine arm with power. Thine hand be made steadfast, and thy right hand be enhanced;
89.14: rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]] and doom is the making ready of thy seat. Mercy and truth shall go before thy face;
89.15: blessed is the people that know a hearty song. Lord, they shall go in the light of thy cheer;
89.16: and in thy name they shall make full out joy all day; and they shall be enhanced in thy rightfulness [[or right-wiseness]].
89.17: For thou art the glory of the virtue of them; and in thy good pleasance our horn shall be enhanced.
89.18: For our taking up is of the Lord; and of the Holy of Israel our king.
89.19: Then thou spakest in revelation to thy saints, and saidest, I have set [[or put]] help in the mighty; and I have enhanced the chosen man of my people.
89.20: I found David, my servant; I anointed him with mine holy oil.
89.21: For mine hand shall help him; and mine arm shall confirm him.
89.22: The enemy shall nothing profit in him; and the son of wickedness shall not lay to or put to, for to annoy him.
89.23: And I shall slay his enemies from his face; and I shall turn into flight them that hate him.
89.24: And my truth and mercy shall be with him; and his horn shall be enhanced in my name.
89.25: And I shall set [[or put]] his hand in the sea; and his right hand in floods.
89.26: He shall inwardly call me, Thou art my father; my God, and the up-taker of mine health.
89.27: And I shall set him the first be-gotten son; higher than the kings of earth.
89.28: Without end I shall keep my mercy to him; and my testament faithful to him.
89.29: And I shall set his seed into the world of world; and his throne as the days of heaven.
89.30: Forsooth if his sons forsake my law; and go not in my dooms.
89.31: If they make unholy my rightful-nesses; and keep not my command-ments.
89.32: I shall visit in a rod the wicked-nesses of them; and in beatings the sins of them.
89.33: But I shall not scatter my mercy from him; and in my truth I shall not annoy him.
89.34: Neither I shall make unholy my testament; and I shall not make void those things that come forth of my lips.
89.35: Once I swore in mine holiness, I shall not lie to David;
89.36: his seed shall dwell without end. And his throne as [[the]] sun in my sight,
89.37: and as a perfect moon without end; and a faithful witness in heaven.
89.38: But thou hast put away, and despised; and hast delayed thy christ.
89.39: Thou hast turned away the testa-ment of thy servant; thou madest unholy his saintuary in earth.
89.40: Thou destroyedest all the hedges thereof; thou hast set the steadfastness thereof into dread.
89.41: All men passing by the way ravished him; he is made a shame to his neighbours.
89.42: Thou hast enhanced the right hand of men oppressing him; thou hast gladdened all his enemies.
89.43: Thou hast turned away the help of his sword; and thou helpedest not him in battle.
89.44: Thou destroyedest him from cleansing; and thou hast hurled down his seat in [[the]] earth.
89.45: Thou hast made less the days of his time; thou hast beshed him with shame.
89.46: Lord, how long turnest thou away, into the end; shall thine ire burn out as fire?
89.47: Bethink thou what is my substance; for whether thou hast ordained vainly all the sons of men?
89.48: Who is a man, that shall live, and shall not see death; shall he deliver his soul from the hand of hell?
89.49: Lord, where be thine eld [[or old]] mercies; as thou hast sworn to David in thy truth?
89.50: Lord, be thou mindful of the shame of thy servants; of the insults of many heathen men, which I held together in my bosom.
89.51: Which thine enemies, Lord, did shamefully; for they despised the changing of thy christ.
89.52: Blessed be the Lord without end; be it done, be it done.

90.1: The prayer of Moses, the man of God. Lord, thou art made help to us; from generation into generation.
90.2: Before that hills were made, either the earth and the world was formed; from the world and into the world, thou art God.
90.3: Turn thou not away a man into lowness; and thou saidest, Ye sons of men, be turned again.
90.4: For a thousand years be before thine eyes; as yesterday, which is passed, and as [[the]] keeping in the night.
90.5: The years of them shall be; that be had for nought. Early pass he, as an herb,
90.6: early flourish he, and pass; in the eventide fall he down, be he hard, and wax he dry.
90.7: For we have failed in thine ire; and we be troubled in thy strong vengeance.
90.8: Thou hast set [[or put]] our wicked-nesses in thy sight; our world in the lightening of thy cheer.
90.9: For all our days have failed; and we have failed in thine ire. Our years we shall bethink upon as a spider;
90.10: the days of our years be those seventy years. Forsooth, if fourscore or eighty years be in mighty men; and the more time of them is travail and sorrow. For mildness came above; and we shall be chastised.
90.11: Who knew the power of thine ire; and durst number thine ire for thy dread?
90.12: Make thy right hand so known; and make men learned in heart by wisdom.
90.13: Lord, be thou converted some-deal; and be thou able to be prayed of by thy servants.
90.14: We were [[ful]] filled early with thy mercy; we made full out joy, and we delighted in all our days.
90.15: We were glad for the days in which thou madest us meek; for the years in which we saw evils.
